## Introduction

Electron library is a Robot Framework library for testing Electron applications.


It is built on the [Browser library](https://robotframework-browser.org): its keywords, such as [Click](#click) and [Get Text](#get-text), act on the windows of an application. Import `Electron` instead of `Browser`. The library hides Browser's keywords for browsers and contexts, see [Browser, Context and Page](#browser-context-and-page). Guides and examples are on the [documentation site](https://robotcodedev.github.io/robotframework-electron-vscode/).


### Starting and closing an application

[Start Electron Application](#start-electron-application) starts an application and waits for its first window. Pass the application's executable, or for an application that the plain Electron binary runs, the Electron executable and the application folder in `args`. The library downloads nothing: the npm package `electron`, for example, brings an Electron release, and `require('electron')` returns its executable.


```text
${app}    ${page} =    `Start Electron Application`    /opt/my-app/my-app
`Get Title`    ==    My App
`Click`    text=Settings
```

[Close Electron Application](#close-electron-application) ends an application. Automatic closing ends it with the test or suite that started it, see [Automatic page and context closing](#automatic-page-and-context-closing).


Each window of an application is a page for Browser keywords, see [Windows and pages](#windows-and-pages).


### Several applications

Several applications can be open at once. [Switch Electron Application](#switch-electron-application) makes another one the active application, and [Get Electron Application Ids](#get-electron-application-ids) returns their ids.


### The main process

Browser keywords reach the windows, but not the application's main process. [Evaluate In Main Process](#evaluate-in-main-process) runs a JavaScript function there, for example to replace a native dialog or click a menu item. [Set Window Size](#set-window-size), [Maximize Window](#maximize-window) and the other window keywords size windows and change their state, see [Windows and pages](#windows-and-pages).


### Launch options

[Start Electron Application](#start-electron-application) takes some options of the Browser library's `New Context`: `color_scheme`, `locale`, `timezone_id` and `bypass_csp`. They apply from the start, so another value means starting the application again.


### Videos, traces and HAR files

[Start Electron Application](#start-electron-application) records a video of the windows with `record_video`, a Playwright trace with `tracing`, and the network traffic of the windows with `record_har`. They are saved when the application closes.


### Browser, Context and Page

The Browser library organises web pages in browsers, contexts and pages, see [Browser, Context and Page](https://marketsquare.github.io/robotframework-browser/Browser.html#Browser%2C%20Context%20and%20Page) in its documentation. An application maps onto them as follows:


- An application is a browser of its own with exactly one context. The id that [Start Electron Application](#start-electron-application) returns is the application id.
- Each window of the application is a page, and so is each `\<webview>` and `WebContentsView`. [Switch Page](#switch-page) and [Get Page Ids](#get-page-ids) work on all of them, [Get Window Ids](#get-window-ids) lists only the windows, see [Windows and pages](#windows-and-pages). [Close Page](#close-page) closes windows and the pages of a `WebContentsView`. On the page of a `\<webview>`, it waits forever, so a test removes the `\<webview>` element from its page instead.


#### Compared with the Browser library

The library hides the Browser keywords for browsers and contexts, and those that cannot work on an application:


| Browser keyword | Here | Why |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `New Browser`, `New Persistent Context`, `Open Browser` | [Start Electron Application](#start-electron-application) | A test starts an application. |
| `Close Browser`, `Close Context` | [Close Electron Application](#close-electron-application) | The application ends with its only context. |
| `Switch Browser` | [Switch Electron Application](#switch-electron-application) | Several applications can be open at once. |
| `Get Browser Ids` | [Get Electron Application Ids](#get-electron-application-ids) | It returns the ids of the open applications. |
| `Get Browser Catalog` | [Get Electron Application Catalog](#get-electron-application-catalog) | It leaves out the context level. |
| `New Context`, `Switch Context`, `Get Context Ids` | - | An application has exactly one context. |
| `New Page` | - | The application opens its windows itself. |
| `Launch Browser Server`, `Close Browser Server`, `Connect To Browser` | - | For browsers only. |
| `Get Device`, `Get Devices` | - | Devices are options for `New Context`. |
| `Crawl Site` | - | It opens pages of its own. |
| `Set Storage State` | - | It needs a page of its own to write the storage. |
| `Tap` | - | Touch input is not enabled for applications. |
| `Save Page As Pdf` | - | Electron does not provide Chromium's PDF printing over the DevTools protocol. |


A test that needs a web browser as well imports the Browser library beside this one and calls the keywords that both libraries have with the library name, for example `Browser.New Page`.


### Windows and pages

Each window of an application is a page, and so is each `\<webview>` and `WebContentsView` that it shows. After [Start Electron Application](#start-electron-application), the first window is the active page. [Switch Window](#switch-window) makes the page of another window the active page, best by the window's title, because it waits until a window shows it. [Get Electron Application Catalog](#get-electron-application-catalog) lists all pages with their titles, and [Switch Page](#switch-page) selects any of them, also a `\<webview>` or `WebContentsView`.


[Get Window Ids](#get-window-ids) and [Get Window Titles](#get-window-titles) list only the windows. The keywords that act on a window take it in one of these forms:


| Form | Window |
| :--- | :--- |
| `title=\<title>` | The window that shows this title, exactly as [Get Window Titles](#get-window-titles) returns it. |
| `title=/\<pattern>/\<flags>` | The window whose title matches this JavaScript regular expression, in the form of Browser's `text=` selector, for example `title=/^Settings/i`. |
| `window=\<n>` | The window with this id from [Get Window Ids](#get-window-ids). The bare number works as well, because Robot Framework reads `window=2` as the named argument `window` with the value `2`. |
| none | The window that shows the active page, which for a `\<webview>` or `WebContentsView` is around it. |


For a title or an expression, the keywords wait up to the library timeout until exactly one window matches, so a test can name a window that is still opening. Window ids are valid while the application runs and unique only within it, so get them again after [Switch Electron Application](#switch-electron-application).


### Finding elements

Selectors work as in the Browser library, see [Finding elements](https://marketsquare.github.io/robotframework-browser/Browser.html#Finding%20elements) in its documentation. In an application:


- CSS, `id=` and `text=` find elements in open shadow roots, and `>>>` reaches into iframes.
- `>>>` does not reach into a `\<webview>`, which is not an iframe. Switch to the page of the `\<webview>` instead.


### Assertions

Keywords such as [Get Text](#get-text) take an assertion operator and an expected value, and retry until the assertion holds or the timeout has passed, see [Assertions](https://marketsquare.github.io/robotframework-browser/Browser.html#Assertions) in the Browser library's documentation.


### Implicit waiting

Browser keywords wait until their elements are ready, see [Implicit waiting](https://marketsquare.github.io/robotframework-browser/Browser.html#Implicit%20waiting) in the Browser library's documentation. [Set Browser Timeout](#set-browser-timeout) changes how long.


### Scope Setting

Keywords that change a setting, such as [Set Browser Timeout](#set-browser-timeout), take a scope that says how long the setting lasts, see [Scope Setting](https://marketsquare.github.io/robotframework-browser/Browser.html#Scope%20Setting) in the Browser library's documentation.


### Automatic page and context closing

An application ends with the test or suite that started it, as the Browser library closes browsers and contexts, see [Automatic page and context closing](https://marketsquare.github.io/robotframework-browser/Browser.html#Automatic%20page%20and%20context%20closing) in its documentation. [Close Electron Application](#close-electron-application) ends it earlier.

#### Documentation:
Electron library takes the same import arguments as the Browser library, described under [Importing](https://marketsquare.github.io/robotframework-browser/Browser.html#Importing) in its documentation.


They configure the Browser keywords, for example their timeout or presenter mode, and apply to the windows of applications as to any other page. Arguments that are about browsers, such as `external_browser_executable`, have no effect on applications. All arguments are named arguments.


Example:


```text
Library    Electron    timeout=20s    enable_presenter_mode=True
```

### Add Cookie

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `name`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Name of the cookie. |
| `value`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Given value for the cookie. |
| `url`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Given url for the cookie. Defaults to None. Either `url` or the `domain` / `path` pair must be set, but not both. |
| `domain`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Given domain for the cookie. Defaults to None. Either `url` or the `domain` / `path` pair must be set, but not both. |
| `path`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Given path for the cookie. Defaults to None. Either `url` or the `domain` / `path` pair must be set, but not both. |
| `expires`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`datetime`](#datetime-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Given expiry for the cookie. Can be a date, a unix time or a datetime object. Supports the same formats as the [DateTime](http://robotframework.org/robotframework/latest/libraries/DateTime.html) library or an epoch timestamp. Example: `2027-09-28 16:21:35` |
| `httpOnly`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Sets the httpOnly token. |
| `secure`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Sets the secure token. |
| `sameSite`| : [`CookieSameSite`](#cookiesamesite-enum) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Sets the sameSite mode. Can be `Strict`, `Lax` or `None`. |

**Tags**:
- BrowserControl
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Adds a cookie to the currently active browser context.


Example:


```text
`Add Cookie`   foo   bar   http://address.com/path/to/site                                     # Using url argument.
`Add Cookie`   foo   bar   domain=example.com                path=/foo/bar                     # Using domain and path arguments.
`Add Cookie`   foo   bar   http://address.com/path/to/site   expires=2027-09-28 16:21:35       # Expires as timestamp.
`Add Cookie`   foo   bar   http://address.com/path/to/site   expires=1822137695                # Expires as epoch seconds.
```

[Comment >>](https://forum.robotframework.org/t//4233)

### Add Locator Handler Click

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Is the selector to the element which indicates that the locator handler should be called. |
| `click_selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Is the selector to the element to be clicked. |
| `🏷noWaitAfter`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${True}` | Defaults to `True`, which means that the overlay may stay visible after the handler has run. If set to `False`, Playwright waits until the overlay becomes hidden, and only then the library continues with the action/assertion that triggered the handler. |
| `🏷times`| : [`int`](#integer-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Is how many times the locator handler is called. `None`, the default, means unlimited. |
| `🏷click_clickCount`| : [`int`](#integer-standard) | = | `${1}` | Is the number of times to click the element. Defaults to 1. |
| `🏷click_delay`| : [`int`](#integer-standard) | = | `${0}` | Time to wait between mousedown and mouseup in milliseconds. Defaults to 0. |
| `🏷click_force`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | Whether to bypass checks and dispatch the event directly. Defaults to false. |

**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Add a handler function which will activate when `selector` is visible and click.


The handler will click the element indicated by `click_selector`.


When testing a web page, sometimes unexpected overlays, for example an "Accept Cookies" dialog, might appear and block the interaction with the page, like the [Click](#click) keyword. These overlays can be problematic to handle, because they might appear randomly in the page. This keyword allows to create an automatic method, which will close those overlays by clicking the element indicated by `click_selector`. The handler is activated when the element indicated by `selector` is visible. For further information, see Playwright's [addLocatorHandler](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-add-locator-handler) method.


The arguments `click_selector`, `click_clickCount`, `click_delay` and `click_force` correspond to the arguments of the [Click With Options](#click-with-options) keyword, but `click_delay` is given as a plain number of milliseconds. The `selector`, `noWaitAfter` and `times` are for the locator handler. The handler is tied to the active page, if there is need to add handler to another page, this keyword needs to be called separately for each page. If the `times` argument is set to a positive value, the locator handler is removed after the handler has been called the specified number of times.


Example add locator handler to click button with id="ButtonInOverlay" when id=Overlay is visible:


```text
`New Page`    ${URL}
`Add Locator Handler Click`    id=Overlay    id=ButtonInOverlay     # Add locator handler to page
`Type Text`    id:username    user    # If element with id=Overlay appears, the handler will click the button id=ButtonInOverlay
`Type Text`    id:password    password    # Or if overlay is visible here, then handler is called here
`Click`    id:login
`Remove Locator Handler`    id=Overlay    # Removes the locator handler from page
```

### Add Locator Handler Custom

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Is the selector to the element which indicates that the locator handler should be called. |
| `handler_spec`| : [`list`](#list-standard)`[`[`dict`](#dictionary-standard)`]` |  |  | Is a list of dictionaries which defines the actions to be performed. |
| `noWaitAfter`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${True}` | Defaults to `True`, which means that the overlay may stay visible after the handler has run. If set to `False`, Playwright waits until the overlay becomes hidden, and only then the library continues with the action/assertion that triggered the handler. |
| `times`| : [`int`](#integer-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Is how many times the locator handler is called. `None`, the default, means unlimited. |

**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Add a handler function which will activate when `selector` is visible and performs handler specification.


When the element indicated by `selector` is visible, the handler will perform the actions specified in the `handler_spec`.


The `handler_spec` is a list of dictionaries, where each dictionary defines one action. The dictionary must contain the key `action` which defines the action to be performed. The action can be one of the following: [click](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-click), [fill](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-fill), [check](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-check) and [uncheck](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-uncheck). Action is also case insensitive. The dictionary must also contain the key `selector` which defines the element to be interacted with. The `fill` action must also contain the key `value` which defines the value to be filled in the element. For the other actions the key `value` must not be defined. Additional keys are passed to the action as keyword arguments. For example for the [click](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-click) action refer to Playwright's documentation to see which options are possible.


The selectors in the `handler_spec` are not resolved in strict mode. If a selector matches more than one element, the first matching element is used. If an action in the handler fails, the error is only logged on the Browser library node side and the keyword which triggered the handler does not fail because of it.


The `selector`, `noWaitAfter` and `times` are for the locator handler [method](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-add-locator-handler). The handler is tied to the active page, if there is need to add handler to another page, this keyword needs to be called separately for each page. If the `times` argument is set to a positive value, the locator handler is removed after the handler has been called the specified number of times.


Running the handler will alter your page state mid-test. For example it will change the currently focused element and move the mouse. Make sure that keywords that run after the handler are self-contained and do not rely on the focus and mouse state being unchanged.


Please note that the automatic argument conversion is not done for the `handler_spec` dictionary. This is because Robot Framework does not convert values inside the dictionary that are actually arguments to a separate Playwright API call. Therefore the user is responsible for converting the values to the correct type. For example if a timeout is needed, the value must be converted to a number on the Robot Framework test data side.


Example adds locator handler to fill input id=overlayInput with value "Hello" and click element id=OverlayCloseButton when id=Overlay is visible:


```text
`New Page`    ${URL}
VAR    &{handler_spec_fill}
...    action=Fill
...    selector=id=overlayInput
...    value=Hello
VAR    &{handler_spec_click}
...    action=click
...    selector=id=OverlayCloseButton
`Add Locator Handler Custom`
...    id=overlay
...    [${handler_spec_fill}, ${handler_spec_click}]
`Type Text`    id:username    user    # If element with id=overlay appears, the handler fills id=overlayInput and clicks id=OverlayCloseButton
`Type Text`    id:password    password    # Or if overlay is visible here, then handler is called here
`Click`    id:login
```

Example with click and different options and types:


```text
VAR    &{handler_spec}
...    action=CLICK    # Action is case insensitive
...    selector=id=OverlayCloseButton
...    button=left
...    clickCount=${1}
...    delay=${0.1}
...    force=${True}
Add Locator Handler Custom    id=overlay    [${handler_spec}]
```

The keyword can only handle click, fill, check and uncheck Playwright API calls. If there is a need for more complex interactions, it is recommended to create a custom js extension to handle the interactions.


Example:


```text
async function customLocatorHandler(locator, pageLocator, clickLocator, page) {
    console.log("Adding custom locator handler for: " + locator);
    const pageLocator = page.locator(locator).first();
    await page.addLocatorHandler(
        pageLocator,
        async () => {
            console.log("Handling custom locator: " + clickLocator);
            // More complex interactions can be added here
            await page.locator(clickLocator).click();
        }
    );
}
exports.__esModule = true;
exports.customLocatorHandler = customLocatorHandler;
```

### Click

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Selector element to click. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |
| `button`| : [`MouseButton`](#mousebutton-enum) | = | `left` | Mouse button to click with. One of `left`, `middle` or `right`. Defaults to `left`. |

**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Simulates mouse click on the element found by `selector`.


This keyword clicks an element matching `selector` by performing the following steps:


- Find an element matching the selector. If there is none, wait until a matching element is attached to the DOM.
- Wait for actionability checks on the matched element. If the element is detached during the checks, the whole action is retried.
- Scroll the element into view if needed.
- Use [Mouse Button](#mousebutton-enum) to click in the center of the element.
- Wait for initiated navigation to either succeed or fail.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


See [Click With Options](#click-with-options) if you need modifiers, a click count, a click position or want to skip the actionability checks.


Example:


```text
`Click`    id=button_location
`Click`    id=button_location    left
`Click`    id=button_location    right
```

[Comment >>](https://forum.robotframework.org/t//4238)

### Click With Options

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Selector element to click. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |
| `button`| : [`MouseButton`](#mousebutton-enum) | = | `left` | Mouse button to click with. One of `left`, `middle` or `right`. Defaults to `left`. |
| `*modifiers`| : [`KeyboardModifier`](#keyboardmodifier-enum) |  |  | Modifier keys to press. Ensures that only these modifiers are pressed during the click, and then restores current modifiers back. If not specified, currently pressed modifiers are used. Modifiers can be specified in any order, and multiple modifiers can be specified. Valid modifier keys are `Alt`, `Control`, `ControlOrMeta`, `Meta` and `Shift`. Due to the fact that the argument `*modifiers` is a positional only argument, all preceding keyword arguments have to be specified as positional arguments before `*modifiers`. |
| `🏷clickCount`| : [`int`](#integer-standard) | = | `${1}` | How many times the button is clicked. Defaults to 1. |
| `🏷delay`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Time to wait between mouse-down and mouse-up. Defaults to no delay. |
| `🏷force`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | Set to `True` to skip Playwright's Actionability checks ([https://playwright.dev/docs/actionability](https://playwright.dev/docs/actionability)). Defaults to `False`. |
| `🏷noWaitAfter`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | Deprecated. This option will default to true in the future. Actions that initiate navigation, are waiting for these navigation to happen and for pages to start loading. You can opt out of waiting via setting this flag. You would only need this option in the exceptional cases such as navigating to inaccessible pages. Defaults to `False`. |
| `🏷position_x`| : [`float`](#float-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | A point to click relative to the top-left corner of element bounding-box. Only positive values within the bounding-box are allowed. Both values must be given, otherwise the position is ignored. If not specified, clicks to some visible point of the element. |
| `🏷position_y`| : [`float`](#float-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | A point to click relative to the top-left corner of element bounding-box. Only positive values within the bounding-box are allowed. Both values must be given, otherwise the position is ignored. If not specified, clicks to some visible point of the element. |
| `🏷trial`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | When set, this method only performs the actionability checks and skips the action. Defaults to `False`. Useful to wait until the element is ready for the action without performing it. |

**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Simulates mouse click on the element found by `selector`.


This keyword clicks an element matching `selector` by performing the following steps:


- Find an element matching the selector. If there is none, wait until a matching element is attached to the DOM.
- Wait for actionability checks on the matched element, unless the `force` option is set. If the element is detached during the checks, the whole action is retried.
- Scroll the element into view if needed.
- Use [Mouse Button](#mousebutton-enum) to click in the center of the element, or the specified position.
- Wait for initiated navigation to either succeed or fail, unless the `noWaitAfter` option is set.


Arguments `clickCount`, `delay`, `position_x`, `position_y`, `force`, `noWaitAfter` and `trial` are named-only arguments and must be specified using their names.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


Example:


```text
`Click With Options`    id=button_location
`Click With Options`    id=button_location    trial=True
`Click With Options`    \#clickWithOptions    delay=100ms    clickCount=2
`Click With Options`    id=clickWithModifiers    left     Alt    Meta    Shift    clickCount=1    force=True
`Click With Options`    id=clickWithOptions    right    clickCount=2    force=True
```

### Close Electron Application

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|

**Return Type**: [`None`](#none-standard)


#### Documentation:
Ends an Electron application and removes it from the library state.


The keyword returns after the application process has exited. It also passes if the application has already quit on its own. The application that was active before becomes active again. Automatic closing ends applications as well, see [Automatic page and context closing](#automatic-page-and-context-closing).


Example:


```text
${app}    ${_} =    `Start Electron Application`    /opt/my-app/my-app
`Close Electron Application`    ${app}
`Close Electron Application`    ALL
```

### Close Page

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `page`| : [`SelectionType`](#selectiontype-enum) \| [`NewPageDetails`](#newpagedetails-typeddict) \| [`str`](#string-standard) | = | `CURRENT` | Page to close. `CURRENT` selects the active page. `ALL` selects all pages. When a page id is provided, that page is closed. |
| `context`| : [`SelectionType`](#selectiontype-enum) \| [`str`](#string-standard) | = | `CURRENT` | Context in which pages are closed. `CURRENT` selects the active context. `ALL` selects all contexts. When a context id is provided, pages of that context are closed. The contexts themselves are not closed. |
| `browser`| : [`SelectionType`](#selectiontype-enum) \| [`str`](#string-standard) | = | `CURRENT` | Browser in which pages are closed. `CURRENT` selects the active browser. `ALL` selects all browsers. When a browser id is provided, pages of that browser are closed. The browsers themselves are not closed. |
| `runBeforeUnload`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | defines whether to run the [before unload](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Window/beforeunload_event) page handlers. Defaults to false. |

**Return Type**: [`list`](#list-standard)`[`[`dict`](#dictionary-standard)`]`


**Tags**:
- BrowserControl
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Closes the `page` in `context` in `browser`.


Defaults to current for all three. Active page is set to the page that was active before this one. See [Browser, Context and Page](#browser-context-and-page) for more information about Page and related concepts.


If a page id is given, the `context` and `browser` arguments are ignored and the page is searched from all open browsers. Likewise, if a context id is given, the `browser` argument is ignored.


Returns a list of dictionaries containing id, errors and console messages from the page.


Example:


```text
`Close Page`                                       # Closes current page, within the current context and browser
`Close Page`    CURRENT     CURRENT     CURRENT    # Closes current page, within the current context and browser
`Close Page`    ALL         ALL         ALL        # Closes all pages, within all contexts and browsers
```

[Comment >>](https://forum.robotframework.org/t//4241)


**In Electron applications:**


Closes windows and the pages of a `WebContentsView`. On the page of a `\<webview>`, it waits forever: Electron destroys the contents of the `\<webview>`, but Chromium reports the page as closed only once the `\<webview>` element is gone. Remove the element instead:


```text
`Evaluate JavaScript`    id=guest    (element) => element.remove()
```

An application has exactly one context, and `browser` takes an application id, see [Browser, Context and Page](#browser-context-and-page).

### Create Credential

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `rpId`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Relying party id (typically the site's effective domain). |
| `id_`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Base64url-encoded credential id. Auto-generated if omitted. |
| `privateKey`| : [`Secret`](#secret-standard) \| [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Base64url-encoded PKCS\#8 (DER) private key. Auto-generated if omitted. |
| `publicKey`| : [`Secret`](#secret-standard) \| [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Base64url-encoded SPKI (DER) public key. Auto-generated if omitted. |
| `userHandle`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Base64url-encoded user handle. Auto-generated if omitted. |

**Tags**:
- Credential
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Creates a credential with the given parameters.


Will always [create](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-credentials#credentials-create) and [install](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-credentials#credentials-install) the credential, even if the optional parameters are not provided. In this case Playwright will autogenerate the missing values.


The credential is created in the currently active context and it is used by all pages that are created from that context. There must be an open context, otherwise the keyword fails.


Because `privateKey` and `publicKey` are sensitive information, it is recommended to wrap their values in the Secret type. The Secret type requires Robot Framework 7.4 or newer. If you are using Robot Framework 7.3 or older, the keyword supports resolving `privateKey` and `publicKey` from Robot Framework variables and environment variables in the following ways. The keyword resolves the value from a Robot Framework variable internally, when the variable is prefixed with `$`, without the curly braces. Example: `$publicKey` will resolve to the `${publicKey}` Robot Framework variable.


If the `privateKey` or `publicKey` value is prefixed with `%`, the library will resolve the corresponding environment variable. Example: `%PUBLICKEY` will resolve to the `%{PUBLICKEY}` environment variable.


Plain values are not accepted. If the given `privateKey` or `publicKey` is not a Secret and does not resolve to another value, the keyword fails with an error stating that direct assignment of values or variables is not allowed.


Example:


```text
`New Context`
${credentials} =    Get Credentials   # This is a helper keyword that returns a dictionary with the required credential parameters.
`Create Credential`
...    rpId=${DOMAIN_NAME}
...    id_=${credentials["id"]}
...    privateKey=${credentials["privateKey"]}    # This should be a Secret type or a string starting with $ which resolves to a Robot Framework variable.
...    publicKey=${credentials["publicKey"]}    # This should be a Secret type or a string starting with $ which resolves to a Robot Framework variable.
...    userHandle=${credentials["userHandle"]}
`New Page`    ${SUT_URL}
`Click`    id=login
`Get Text`    id=status    ==    Success
```

### Download

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `url`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | URL to the file that shall be downloaded. |
| `saveAs`| : [`str`](#string-standard) | = | `${EMPTY}` | Path where the file shall be saved persistently. If empty, generated unique path (GUID) is used and file is deleted when the context is closed. |
| `wait_for_finished`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${True}` | If set to `False` keyword returns immediately after the download has started. Defaults to `True`. |
| `download_timeout`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Maximum total time for the file to be fetched and saved. If the file is not fetched within this time, the keyword fails. If it is fetched but not saved, the download is cancelled and the keyword fails. If `wait_for_finished` is `False`, only the fetching is limited. If not set, the file must be fetched within the browser timeout, see [Set Browser Timeout](#set-browser-timeout), and there is no limit for saving it. |

**Return Type**: [`DownloadInfo`](#downloadinfo-typeddict)


**Tags**:
- Page Content

#### Documentation:
Download given url content.


Keyword returns dictionary of type [DownloadInfo](#downloadinfo-typeddict).


Example:


```text
{
  "saveAs": "/tmp/robotframework-browser/downloads/2f1b3b7c-1b1b-4b1b-9b1b-1b1b1b1b1b1b",
  "suggestedFilename": "downloaded_file.txt",
  "state": "finished",
  "downloadID": None,
}
```

When `wait_for_finished` is `False`, the returned dictionary has an empty `saveAs`, the `state` is `in_progress` and `downloadID` contains the id of the download. The download can then be followed with the [Get Download State](#get-download-state) keyword, which also saves the file to `saveAs` when the download is finished.


If the download should be started by an interaction with an element on the page, [Promise To Wait For Download](#promise-to-wait-for-download) keyword may be a better choice.


The keyword `New Browser` has a `downloadsPath` setting which can be used to set the default download directory. If `saveAs` is set to a relative path, the file will be saved relative to the browser's `downloadsPath` setting or if that is not set, relative to the Playwright's working directory. If `saveAs` is set to an absolute path, the file will be saved to that absolute path independent of `downloadsPath`.


To enable downloads context's `acceptDownloads` needs to be true, otherwise the keyword fails. This keyword requires that there is currently an open page and that the page has been navigated to an url, downloading from `about:blank` fails. The download is done by a `fetch` call inside the page and therefore it uses the current page's local state (cookies, sessionstorage, localstorage) to avoid authentication problems. Because of that, a relative `url` is resolved against the current page url and the page's cross-origin restrictions apply.


The whole file is fetched before the browser reports the download as started. Set `download_timeout` when fetching the file can take longer than the browser timeout, for example with large files or slow servers.


Example:


```text
${file_object}=    `Download`    ${url}    download_timeout=2 minutes
${actual_size}=    Get File Size    ${file_object.saveAs}
```

Example 2:


```text
${href}=          `Get Property`    text="Download File"    href
`Download`    ${href}    saveAs=${OUTPUT DIR}/downloads/downloaded_file.txt
File Should Exist    ${OUTPUT DIR}/downloads/downloaded_file.txt
```

### Drag And Drop

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector_from`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Identifies the element whose center is the start-point. |

#### Documentation:
Executes a Drag&Drop operation from the element selected by `selector_from` to the element selected by `selector_to`.


See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors.


First it moves the mouse to the start-point, then presses the left mouse button, then moves to the end-point in specified number of steps, then releases the mouse button.


Start- and end-point are defined by the center of the elements' bounding box.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


Example


```text
`Drag And Drop`    "Circle"    "Goal"
```

First it moves the mouse to the start-point, then presses the left mouse button, then moves to the end-point in specified number of steps, then releases the mouse button.


Start- and end-point are defined by `x` and `y` coordinates relative to the top left corner of the pages viewport.

#### Arguments:

| `forcedColors`| : [`ForcedColors`](#forcedcolors-enum) \| [`NotSet`](#notset-enum) | = | `not_set` | Emulates the `forced-colors` media feature, supported values are `active` and `none`. Passing `null` disables forced colors emulation. |

| `reducedMotion`| : [`ReducedMotion`](#reducedmotion-enum) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Emulates the `prefers-reduced-motion` media feature, supported values are `reduce` and `no-preference`. Passing `null` disables reduced motion emulation. |

### Evaluate In Main Process

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `function`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | A JavaScript function as text, or its first line. The function gets three parameters: the `electron` module, `arg`, and `window`, the `BrowserWindow` that shows the active page. For a `\<webview>` or a `WebContentsView`, that is the window they are shown in. `window` is `null` if the active page is not one of the application's, for example while another application is active. The function may return a promise. |
| `*lines`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Further lines of the function. They are joined to `function` with line breaks, so that a function can span several cells with `...`. |
| `🏷arg`| : [`Any`](#any-standard) | = | `${None}` | A JSON-serialisable value that the function gets. |
| `🏷application`| : [`SelectionType`](#selectiontype-enum) \| [`str`](#string-standard) | = | `CURRENT` | `CURRENT` for the active application, or an application id that [Start Electron Application](#start-electron-application) returned. |

**Return Type**: [`Any`](#any-standard) — The function's result, which must be JSON-serialisable. Objects of the main process, such as a `BrowserWindow`, cannot be returned. `None` if the function returns nothing.


**Raises**:
- `AssertionError`: No application is open, the id is not an application started by [Start Electron Application](#start-electron-application), or the function throws an error.


#### Documentation:
Runs a JavaScript function in the main process of an Electron application and returns its result.


Browser keywords reach the application's windows, but not its main process. There, a test can replace a native dialog before the application opens it, focus a window, click a menu item, or read the application's state. The window keywords, such as [Set Window Size](#set-window-size) and [Maximize Window](#maximize-window), size windows and change their state. The function runs as with Playwright's `electronApplication.evaluate`.


Example:


```text
${name} =    `Evaluate In Main Process`    ({ app }) => app.getName()
`Evaluate In Main Process`    ({ dialog }, path) => {
...        dialog.showOpenDialog = async () => ({ canceled: false, filePaths: [path] });
...    }
...    arg=${EXECDIR}/data/report.csv
${focused} =    `Evaluate In Main Process`    (electron, arg, window) => window.isFocused()
```

### Evaluate JavaScript

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Selector to resolve and pass to the JavaScript function. This will be the first argument the function receives if not `${None}`. `selector` is optional and can be omitted. If given a selector, a function is necessary, with an argument to capture the element. For example `(element) => document.activeElement === element`. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |
| `*function`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | A valid javascript function or a javascript function body. These arguments can be used to write readable multiline JavaScript. |
| `🏷arg`| : [`Any`](#any-standard) | = | `${None}` | an additional argument that can be handed over to the JavaScript function. It is the second argument of the function when a `selector` is given, otherwise the first one. This argument must be JSON serializable. ElementHandles are not supported. |
| `🏷all_elements`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | defines if only the single element found by `selector` is handed over to the function or if set to `True` all found elements are handed over as array. |

**Return Type**: [`Any`](#any-standard)


**Tags**:
- Getter
- PageContent
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Executes the given JavaScript in the browser page.


The JavaScript is evaluated in the context of the page, not in the Node process of the library. Therefore browser globals like `window` and `document` are available, but Robot Framework variables and Python objects are not. Only `arg` and the resolved element(s) are passed into the page.


The value returned by the JavaScript is transferred as JSON and must therefore be JSON serializable. DOM nodes and other non serializable objects can not be returned. If the JavaScript does not return anything, the keyword returns an empty string.


Example with `all_elements=True`:


```text
 ${texts}=    Evaluate JavaScript    button
 ...    (elements, arg) => {
 ...        let text = []
 ...            for (e of elements) {
 ...                console.log(e.innerText)
 ...                text.push(e.innerText)
 ...            }
 ...        text.push(arg)
 ...        return text
 ...    }
 ...    all_elements=True
 ...    arg=Just another Text
```

Keyword uses strict mode only if `all_elements` is `False`. See [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


[Usage examples.](https://github.com/MarketSquare/robotframework-browser/tree/main/atest/test/06_Examples/js_evaluation.robot)

### Fill Secret

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Selector of the text field. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |
| `secret`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`Secret`](#secret-standard) |  |  | The secret string that should be filled into the text field. Supports Robot Framework 7.4 Secret type as normal variable (with curly braces). Also environment variable name with % prefix or a local variable with $ prefix that has the secret text value (without curly braces). |
| `force`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | Set to `True` to skip Playwright's [Actionability checks](https://playwright.dev/docs/actionability). |

**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Fills the given `secret` into the text field found by `selector`.


This keyword does not log the secret in Robot Framework logs, but if Playwright debug logs are enabled, the secret will be visible as plain text in the Playwright debug logs, regardless of the Robot Framework log level or how `secret` is resolved.


This keyword supports Robot Framework 7.4 [Secret](https://robotframework.org/robotframework/latest/RobotFrameworkUserGuide.html#secret-variables) variable type, which is the recommended way if you are using Robot Framework 7.4 or newer.


For older Robot Framework versions the keyword supports resolving secrets from environment variables and Robot Framework variables in the following ways. The keyword resolves the `secret` from a Robot Framework variable internally, when the `secret` variable is prefixed with `$`, without the curly braces. Example: `$Password` will resolve to the `${Password}` Robot Framework variable.


If the `secret` variable is prefixed with `%`, the library will resolve the corresponding environment variable. Example: `%ENV_PWD` will resolve to the `%{ENV_PWD}` environment variable.


**Using normal Robot Framework variables like `${password}`, which are not Secret type variables, will not work!**


**Normal plain text will not work.** If you want to use plain text, use the [Fill Text](#fill-text) keyword instead.


This keyword also works with a cryptographic cipher text that has been encrypted by CryptoLibrary. See [CryptoLibrary](https://github.com/Snooz82/robotframework-crypto) for more details.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


See [Fill Text](#fill-text) for other details.


Example:


```text
`Fill Secret`    input#username_field    ${username}    # Keyword resolves variable value from Robot Framework Secret type variables
`Fill Secret`    input#username_field    $username      # Keyword resolves variable value from Robot Framework variables
`Fill Secret`    input#username_field    %username      # Keyword resolves variable value from environment variables
```

### Fill Text

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Selector of the text field. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |
| `txt`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Text for the text field. |
| `force`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | Set to `True` to skip Playwright's [Actionability checks](https://playwright.dev/docs/actionability). |

**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Clears and fills the given `txt` into the text field found by `selector`.


This keyword waits for an element matching the `selector` to appear, waits for actionability checks, focuses the element, fills it and triggers an input event after filling.


If the element matching the selector is not an \<input>, \<textarea> or [contenteditable] element, this keyword fails. Note that you can pass an empty string as `txt` to clear the input field.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


See [Type Text](#type-text) for emulating typing text character by character.


Example:


```text
`Fill Text`    css=input#username_field    username
```

**Tags**:

#### Documentation:
Moves focus on to the element found by `selector`.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


If there is no element matching the selector, the keyword waits until a matching element appears in the DOM. It fails if the element does not appear within the library timeout, which is 10 seconds by default and can be changed with [Set Browser Timeout](#set-browser-timeout).

### Get Aria Snapshot

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Selector from which the info is to be retrieved. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |
| `return_type`| : [`AriaSnapshotReturnType`](#ariasnapshotreturntype-enum) | = | `yaml` | Defines the return type. Possible values are `yaml` (default), `dict` and `parsed`. If `yaml` is selected, the returned value is a string in YAML format. If `dict` is selected, the returned value is a dictionary. If `parsed` is selected, the returned value is a tree of node dictionaries. |
| `assertion_operator`| : [`AssertionOperator`](#assertionoperator-enum) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | See [Assertions](#assertions) for further details. Defaults to None. |
| `assertion_expected`| : [`Any`](#any-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Expected value for the state |
| `message`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | overrides the default error message for assertion. |
| `🏷mode`| : [`AriaSnapshotMode`](#ariasnapshotmode-enum) | = | `default` | Defines the snapshot mode. Possible values are `default` (default) and `ai`. See [AriaSnapshotMode](#ariasnapshotmode-enum) for more details. |
| `🏷depth`| : [`int`](#integer-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Limits the snapshot to the given number of tree levels. Must be a positive integer. Defaults to `None`, which does not limit the depth. |
| `🏷boxes`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | If `True`, the bounding box of each element is appended to its line as `[box=x,y,width,height]`. Coordinates are relative to the viewport, in CSS pixels. Defaults to `False`. |

**Return Type**: [`str`](#string-standard) | [`dict`](#dictionary-standard) | [`list`](#list-standard) | [`tuple`](#tuple-standard)


**Tags**:
- Assertion
- Getter
- PageContent

#### Documentation:
Returns the aria snapshot of the element found by `selector`. See [AriaSnapshotReturnType](#ariasnapshotreturntype-enum) for more details and examples.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


With `mode=ai` the snapshot is optimized for AI consumption: it contains element references like `[ref=e2]` and the content of iframes inside the element. It also does not wait for a matching element, but fails immediately when no element matches, instead of failing with a timeout like the `default` mode does.


With `return_type=dict` the YAML returned by Playwright is loaded as is. The `[ref=...]` and `[box=...]` annotations are therefore part of the dictionary keys, not separate entries. Use `return_type=parsed` to get them as separate values of each node.


Optionally asserts that the snapshot matches the specified assertion. See [Assertions](#assertions) for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.


Example:


```text
${aria} =    `Get Aria Snapshot`    id=main   # returns YAML string
Log Many    ${aria}
${aria_dict} =    `Get Aria Snapshot`    id=main    dict   # returns dictionary
Log Many    ${aria_dict}
```

### Get Attribute

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Selector from which the info is to be retrieved. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |
| `attribute`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Requested attribute name. |
| `assertion_operator`| : [`AssertionOperator`](#assertionoperator-enum) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | See [Assertions](#assertions) for further details. Defaults to None. |
| `assertion_expected`| : [`Any`](#any-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Expected value for the state |
| `message`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | overrides the default error message for assertion. |

**Return Type**: [`str`](#string-standard) | [`tuple`](#tuple-standard) | [`dict`](#dictionary-standard) | [`None`](#none-standard)


**Tags**:
- Assertion
- Getter
- PageContent

#### Documentation:
Returns the HTML `attribute` of the element found by `selector`.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


Optionally asserts that the attribute value matches the expected value. See [Assertions](#assertions) for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.


When an attribute is selected that is not present and no assertion operator is set, the keyword fails. If an assertion operator is set and the attribute is not present, the returned value is `None`. This can be used to check the presence or the absence of an attribute.


Example Element:


```text
<button class="login button active" id="enabled_button" something>Login</button>
```

Example Code:


```text
`Get Attribute`   id=enabled_button    disabled                   # FAIL => "Attribute 'disabled' not found!"
`Get Attribute`   id=enabled_button    disabled     ==    ${None}     # PASS => returns: None
`Get Attribute`   id=enabled_button    something    evaluate    value is not None    # PASS =>  returns: True
`Get Attribute`   id=enabled_button    disabled     evaluate    value is None        # PASS =>  returns: True
```

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|

| `assertion_operator`| : [`AssertionOperator`](#assertionoperator-enum) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | See [Assertions](#assertions) for further details. Defaults to None. |
| `*assertion_expected`|   |  |  | Expected value for the state |
| `🏷message`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | overrides the default error message for assertion. |

**Return Type**: [`list`](#list-standard)`[`[`str`](#string-standard)`]`


**Tags**:
- Assertion
- Getter
- PageContent

#### Documentation:
Returns all HTML attribute names of an element as a list.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


Optionally asserts that the attribute names match the expected values. See [Assertions](#assertions) for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.


Available assertions:


- `==` , `!=` and `contains` / `*=` can work with multiple values
- `validate` and `evaluate` only accept one single expected value


Other operators are not allowed.


Example:


```text
`Get Attribute Names`    [name="readonly_input"]    ==    type    name    value    readonly    # Has exactly these attribute names.
`Get Attribute Names`    [name="readonly_input"]    contains    disabled    # Contains at least this attribute name.
```

### Get BoundingBox

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Selector from which the bounding box shall be retrieved. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |
| `key`| : [`BoundingBoxFields`](#boundingboxfields-enum) | = | `ALL` | Optionally filters the returned values. If keys is set to `ALL` (default) it will return the BoundingBox as Dictionary, otherwise it will just return the single value selected by the key. Note: If a single value is retrieved, an assertion does **not** need a `validate` combined with a cast of `value`. |
| `assertion_operator`| : [`AssertionOperator`](#assertionoperator-enum) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | See [Assertions](#assertions) for further details. Defaults to None. |
| `assertion_expected`| : [`Any`](#any-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Expected value for the assertion |
| `message`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | overrides the default error message for assertion. |
| `🏷allow_hidden`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | (named only) If True, hidden elements are not causing a failure and will return `None`. Otherwise a hidden element will fail. Defaults to False. |

**Return Type**: [`BoundingBox`](#boundingbox-typeddict) | [`float`](#float-standard) | [`int`](#integer-standard) | [`None`](#none-standard)


**Tags**:
- Assertion
- Getter
- PageContent

#### Documentation:
Gets elements size and location as an object `{x: float, y: float, width: float, height: float}`.


Alternatively you can select a single attribute of the bounding box by setting the `key` argument.


If an element is hidden and has no bounding box, the keyword will fail. Depending on the method used to make an element invisible, an element might still have a bounding box which can be retrieved. To allow also hidden elements without a bounding box, set `allow_hidden` to `True`, which results in a return value of `None` in case of no bounding box.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


Optionally asserts that the value matches the specified assertion. See [Assertions](#assertions) for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.


Example use:


```text
${bounding_box}=    `Get BoundingBox`    id=element                 # unfiltered
Log                 ${bounding_box}                                 # {'x': 559.09375, 'y': 75.5, 'width': 188.796875, 'height': 18}
${x}=               `Get BoundingBox`    id=element    x            # filtered
Log                 X: ${x}                                         # X: 559.09375
# Assertions:
`Get BoundingBox`     id=element         width         >    180
`Get BoundingBox`     id=element         ALL           validate    value['x'] > value['y']*2
```

### Get Console Log

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `assertion_operator`| : [`AssertionOperator`](#assertionoperator-enum) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Optional assertion operator. See [Assertions](#assertions) for more information. |
| `assertion_expected`| : [`Any`](#any-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Optional expected value. See [Assertions](#assertions) for more information. |
| `message`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Optional custom message to use on failure. See [Assertions](#assertions) for more information. |
| `🏷full`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | If true, returns the full console log. If false, returns only new entries that were added since last time. |
| `🏷last`| : [`int`](#integer-standard) \| [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | If set, returns only the last n entries. Can be an integer for the number of entries or a time period in Robot Framework time format. |

**Return Type**: [`list`](#list-standard)`[`[`dict`](#dictionary-standard)`]`


**Tags**:
- Assertion
- BrowserControl
- Getter

#### Documentation:
Returns the console log of the active page.


If assertions are used and fail, this keyword will fail immediately without retrying.


The returned data is a list of log messages.


A log message is a dictionary with the following structure:


```text
[{
  "type": str,
  "text": str,
  "location": {
    "url": str,
    "lineNumber": int,
    "columnNumber": int
  },
  "time": str
}]
```

Example:


```text
[{
  'type': 'log',
  'text': 'Stuff loaded...',
  'location': {
    'url': 'https://example.com/js/chunk-769742de.6a462276.js',
    'lineNumber': 60,
    'columnNumber': 63771
  },
  'time': '2023-02-05T17:42:52.064Z'
}]
```

Keys:


| Key | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `type` | One of the following values: `log`, `debug`, `info`, `error`, `warning`, `dir`, `dirxml`, `table`, `trace`, `clear`, `startGroup`, `startGroupCollapsed`, `endGroup`, `assert`, `profile`, `profileEnd`, `count`, `timeEnd` |
| `text` | The text of the console message. |
| `location.url` | The URL of the resource that generated this message. |
| `location.lineNumber` | The line number in the resource that generated this message (0-based). |
| `location.columnNumber` | The column number in the resource that generated this message (0-based). |
| `time` | The timestamp of the log message as ISO 8601 string. |

### Get Cookie

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `cookie`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Name of the cookie to be retrieved. |
| `return_type`| : [`CookieType`](#cookietype-enum) | = | `dictionary` | Type of the return value. Can be either `dictionary` or `string`. Defaults to `dictionary`. |

**Return Type**: [`DotDict`](#mapping-standard) | [`str`](#string-standard)


**Tags**:
- BrowserControl
- Getter

#### Documentation:
Returns information about the cookie named `cookie` as a Robot Framework dot dictionary or a string.


If `return_type` is `dictionary` or `dict`, then the keyword returns a Robot Framework [dot dictionary](https://robotframework.org/robotframework/latest/RobotFrameworkUserGuide.html#accessing-list-and-dictionary-items). The dictionary contains all key value pairs of the cookie. If `return_type` is `string` or `str`, then the keyword returns the cookie as a string in format: `name1=value1`. The return value contains only the `name` and `value` keys of the cookie.


If no cookie is found with the given name, the keyword fails. The cookie dictionary contains details about the cookie. Keys available in the dictionary are documented in the table below.


|  |  |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Value** | **Explanation** |
| name | The name of the cookie. |
| value | Value of the cookie. |
| domain | Specifies which hosts are allowed to receive the cookie. |
| path | Indicates a URL path that must exist in the requested URL, for example `/`. |
| expires | Lifetime of a cookie. Returned as a datetime object or None if no valid time is received. |
| httpOnly | When true, the cookie is not accessible via JavaScript. |
| secure | When true, the cookie is only used with HTTPS connections. |
| sameSite | Attribute that lets servers require that a cookie shouldn't be sent with cross-origin requests. |


See [playwright documentation](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-browsercontext#browsercontextaddcookiescookies) for details about each attribute.


Example:


```text
${cookie}=        `Get Cookie`              Foobar
Should Be Equal   ${cookie.value}           Tidii
Should Be Equal   ${cookie.expires.year}     ${2020}
```

[Comment >>](https://forum.robotframework.org/t//4265)

### Get Cookies

#### Arguments:

| | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `return_type`| : [`CookieType`](#cookietype-enum) | = | `dictionary` |

**Return Type**: [`list`](#list-standard)`[`[`DotDict`](#mapping-standard)`]` | [`str`](#string-standard)


**Tags**:
- Getter
- PageContent

#### Documentation:
Returns cookies from the currently active browser context.


If `return_type` is `dictionary` or `dict`, then the keyword returns a list of Robot Framework [dot dictionaries](https://robotframework.org/robotframework/latest/RobotFrameworkUserGuide.html#accessing-list-and-dictionary-items). Each dictionary contains all key value pairs of the cookie. See the [Get Cookie](#get-cookie) keyword documentation for details about the dictionary keys and values.


If `return_type` is `string` or `str`, then the keyword returns the cookies as a string in format: `name1=value1; name2=value2; name3=value3`. The return value contains only `name` and `value` keys of the cookies. If no cookies are found, an empty list is returned.

### Get Credential

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `id_`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Base64url-encoded credential id. |
| `rpId`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Relying party id (typically the site's effective domain). |

**Return Type**: [`ClientCredential`](#clientcredential-typeddict)


**Tags**:
- Credential
- Getter

#### Documentation:
Returns the credential matching the given id and/or rpId.


At least one of `id_` and `rpId` must be given, otherwise the keyword fails. If both are given, the credential must match both of them. When more than one credential matches, the first match is returned. When no credential matches, the keyword fails.


The returned credential is a dictionary with the following keys:


| Key | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| id | Base64url-encoded credential id. |
| rpId | Relying party id (typically the site's effective domain). |
| userHandle | Base64url-encoded user handle. |
| privateKey | Base64url-encoded PKCS\#8 (DER) private key as a Secret. |
| publicKey | Base64url-encoded SPKI (DER) public key as a Secret. |


The privateKey and publicKey are wrapped in the [Secret](https://robotframework.org/robotframework/latest/RobotFrameworkUserGuide.html#secret-variables) type, so that their values are not shown in the Robot Framework log. The values themselves are available in the `value` attribute. Note that the node side of the library might write the whole credential, including the private key, as plain text to the playwright-log.txt file. See [PlaywrightLogTypes](#playwrightlogtypes-enum) for how to control that file.


See [Install Credential](#install-credential) for more information about how to use this keyword.


Example:


```text
${credential} =    `Get Credential`    id_=${CREDENTIAL_ID}
Should Be Equal    ${credential["id"]}    ${CREDENTIAL_ID}
Should Be Equal    ${credential["rpId"]}    ${DOMAIN_NAME}
Should Be Equal    ${credential["userHandle"]}    userhandleCreatedByTheApp
Should Be Equal    ${credential["privateKey"].value}    privateKeyCreatedByTheApp
Should Be Equal    ${credential["publicKey"].value}    publicKeyCreatedByTheApp
```

### Get Electron Application Catalog


**Return Type**: [`list`](#list-standard)`[`[`dict`](#dictionary-standard)`[`[`str`](#string-standard)`, `[`Any`](#any-standard)`]]` — A list with one dictionary per application: its `id`, whether it is the `active` application, and its `pages`. Each page has its `id`, `title`, `url`, and whether it is the `active` page of its application.


#### Documentation:
Returns the open applications with their pages.


Every window, `\<webview>` and `WebContentsView` of an application is a page. The catalog helps to find the page id of one of them for [Switch Page](#switch-page).


Example:


```text
${catalog} =    `Get Electron Application Catalog`
FOR    ${page}    IN    @{catalog}[0][pages]
    Log    ${page}[title]: ${page}[id]
END
```

### Get Element

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Selector from which the element shall be retrieved. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |

**Return Type**: [`str`](#string-standard)


**Tags**:
- Getter
- PageContent

#### Documentation:
Returns a selector string that points to the element found by `selector`.


The returned string is the selector Playwright resolved for the element. It is an ordinary selector, so it can be used as the **first** clause of another selector, chained with `>>`. Because it is a selector and not a captured DOM node, it is resolved again from the page on every use.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


Example:


```text
${element} =    `Get Element`    \#username_field
${option_value} =    `Get Property`    ${element} >> optionOne    value    # Locator is resolved from the page.
${option_value} =    `Get Property`    ${element} >> optionTwo    value    # Locator is resolved again from the page.
```

### Get Element By

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selection_strategy`| : [`SelectionStrategy`](#selectionstrategy-enum) |  |  | SelectionStrategy to be used. Refers to Playwrights `page.getBy***` functions. See [https://playwright.dev/docs/locators](https://playwright.dev/docs/locators) |
| `text`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`RegExp`](#regexp-custom) |  |  | Text to locate the element for. |
| `exact`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | Whether to find an exact match: case-sensitive and whole-string. Defaults to false. Ignored when locating by a regular expression. Note that exact match still trims whitespace. This has no effect if RegExp is used or if TestID is used as strategy. |
| `all_elements`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | If True, returns all matched elements as a list. |

**Return Type**: [`str`](#string-standard)


**Tags**:
- Getter
- PageContent

#### Documentation:
Allows locating elements by their features.


Selection strategies can be several Playwright strategies like AltText or Label. See [Playwright Locators](https://playwright.dev/docs/locators) for more information.


This keywords implements the following Playwright functions:


- [page.getByAltText](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-get-by-alt-text)
- [page.getByLabel](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-get-by-label)
- [page.getByPlaceholder](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-get-by-placeholder)
- [page.getByTestId](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-get-by-test-id)
- [page.getByText](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-get-by-text)
- [page.getByTitle](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-get-by-title)


`page.getByRole` is supported by [Get Element By Role](#get-element-by-role) keyword.


If an element shall be fetched from an iframe, a selector prefix must be set using [Set Selector Prefix](#set-selector-prefix) keyword including `>>>` as ending.

### Get Element By Role

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `role`| : [`ElementRole`](#elementrole-enum) |  |  | Role from which shall be retrieved. |
| `🏷all_elements`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | If True, returns all matched elements as a list. |
| `🏷checked`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | An attribute that is usually set by aria-checked or native \<input type=checkbox> controls. |
| `🏷disabled`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | An attribute that is usually set by aria-disabled or disabled. |
| `🏷exact`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Whether name is matched exactly: case-sensitive and whole-string. Defaults to false. Ignored when name is a regular expression. Note that exact match still trims whitespace. |
| `🏷expanded`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | An attribute that is usually set by aria-expanded. |
| `🏷include_hidden`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Option that controls whether hidden elements are matched. By default, only non-hidden elements, as defined by ARIA, are matched by role selector. |
| `🏷level`| : [`int`](#integer-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | A number attribute that is usually present for roles heading, list item, row, treeitem, with default values for \<h1>-\<h6> elements. |
| `🏷name`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`RegExp`](#regexp-custom) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Option to match the accessible name. By default, matching is case-insensitive and searches for a substring, use exact to control this behavior. |
| `🏷pressed`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | An attribute that is usually set by aria-pressed. |
| `🏷selected`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | An attribute that is usually set by aria-selected. |

**Return Type**: [`str`](#string-standard)


**Tags**:
- Getter
- PageContent

#### Documentation:
Returns a selector string for the element matched by `role`, or a list of selector strings if `all_elements` is set to `True`.


The returned value is used like the one from [Get Element](#get-element): as the first clause of another selector, chained with `>>`.


Allows locating elements by their [ARIA role](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#roles), [ARIA attributes](https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.2/#aria-attributes) and [accessible name](https://w3c.github.io/accname/#dfn-accessible-name).


Consider the following DOM structure.


```text
<h3>Sign up</h3>
<label>
  <input type="checkbox" /> Subscribe
</label>
<br/>
<button>Submit</button>
```

You can locate each element by its implicit role:


```text
${heading}    Get Element By Role    heading    name=Sign up
${checkbox}   Get Element By Role    checkbox    name=Subscribe
${button}     Get Element By Role    button    name=/submit/i
```

If an element shall be fetched from an iframe, a selector prefix must be set using [Set Selector Prefix](#set-selector-prefix) keyword including `>>>` as ending.

### Get Element States

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Selector of the corresponding object. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |
| `assertion_operator`| : [`AssertionOperator`](#assertionoperator-enum) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | See [Assertions](#assertions) for further details. Defaults to None. |
| `*assertion_expected`| : [`ElementState`](#elementstate-enum) \| [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Expected states |
| `🏷message`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | overrides the default error message for assertion. |
| `🏷return_names`|   | = | `${True}` | If set to `False` the keyword does return an IntFlag object ([ElementState](#elementstate-enum)) instead of a list. [ElementState](#elementstate-enum) may contain multiple states at the same time. Defaults to `True`. |

**Return Type**: [`list`](#list-standard)`[`[`str`](#string-standard)`]` | [`ElementState`](#elementstate-enum)


**Tags**:
- Assertion
- Getter
- PageContent

#### Documentation:
Get the active states from the element found by `selector`.


This Keyword returns a list of states that are valid for the selected element.


Optionally asserts that the state matches the specified assertion. See [Assertions](#assertions) for further details for the assertion arguments. By default, assertion is not done.


This keyword internally works with Python IntFlag. Flags can be processed using bitwise operators like & (bitwise AND) and | (bitwise OR). When using the assertion operators `then`, `evaluate` or `validate` the `value` contains the states as [ElementState](#elementstate-enum).


Example:


```text
`Get Element States`    h1    validate    value & visible   # Fails in case of an invisible element
`Get Element States`    h1    then    value & (visible | hidden)  # Returns either ``['visible']`` or ``['hidden']``
`Get Element States`    h1    then    bool(value & visible)  # Returns ``${True}`` if element is visible
```

The most typical use case would be to verify if an element contains a specific state or multiple states.


Example:


```text
`Get Element States`    id=checked_elem      *=    checked
`Get Element States`    id=checked_elem      not contains    checked
`Get Element States`    id=invisible_elem    contains    hidden    attached
`Get Element States`    id=disabled_elem     contains    visible    disabled    readonly
```

Elements do return the positive and negative values if applicable. As example, a checkbox does return either `checked` or `unchecked` while a text input element has none of those two states. Options of select elements have also either `selected` or `deselected`.


If an element is not attached to the DOM, so that it can not be found within 250ms, it is marked as `detached` as the only state.


`stable` state is not returned, because it would cause too high delay in that keyword.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


[Comment >>](https://forum.robotframework.org/t//4272)

### Get Elements

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Selector from which the elements shall be retrieved. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |

**Return Type**: [`list`](#list-standard)`[`[`str`](#string-standard)`]`


**Tags**:
- Getter
- PageContent

#### Documentation:
Returns a list of selector strings, one for each element matched by `selector`.


Each string can be used as the **first** clause of another selector, chained with `>>`, exactly like the value returned by [Get Element](#get-element).


Keyword does not use strict mode and returns an empty list if the `selector` does not match any element.


Example:


```text
${elements} =    `Get Elements`    //select
${elem} =    Get From List    ${elements}    0
${option_value} =    `Get Property`    ${elem} >> option    value
```

### Get Page Errors

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `assertion_operator`| : [`AssertionOperator`](#assertionoperator-enum) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Optional assertion operator. See [Assertions](#assertions) for more information. |
| `assertion_expected`| : [`Any`](#any-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Optional expected value. See [Assertions](#assertions) for more information. |
| `message`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Optional custom message to use on failure. See [Assertions](#assertions) for more information. |
| `🏷full`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | If true, returns all page errors. If false, returns only new errors that were added since last time. |
| `🏷last`| : [`int`](#integer-standard) \| [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | If set, returns only the last n entries. Can be an integer for the number of entries or a time period in Robot Framework time format. |

**Return Type**: [`list`](#list-standard)`[`[`dict`](#dictionary-standard)`]`


**Tags**:
- Assertion
- BrowserControl
- Getter

#### Documentation:
Returns the page errors of the active page.


If assertions are used and fail, this keyword will fail immediately without retrying.


The returned data is a list of error messages.


An error message is a dictionary with the following structure:


```text
{
  "name": str,
  "message": str,
  "stack": str,
  "time": str
}
```

Example:


```text
[{
  'name': 'ReferenceError',
  'message': 'YT is not defined',
  'stack': 'ReferenceError: YT is not defined\n    at HTMLIFrameElement.onload (https://example.com/:20:2245)',
  'time': '2023-02-05T20:08:48.912Z'
}]
```

Keys:


| Key | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `name` | The name/type of the error. |
| `message` | The human readable error message. |
| `stack` | The stack trace of the error, if given. |
| `time` | The timestamp of the error as ISO 8601 string. |
