### Get Page Ids

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `page`| : [`SelectionType`](#selectiontype-enum) | = | `ALL` | The page to get the ids from. `ALL` Returns all page ids as a list. `ACTIVE` Returns the id of the active page as a list. |
| `context`| : [`SelectionType`](#selectiontype-enum) \| [`str`](#string-standard) | = | `ALL` | The context id or selection to get the page ids from. `ALL` Page ids from all contexts shall be fetched. `ACTIVE` Only page ids from the active context shall be fetched. |
| `browser`| : [`SelectionType`](#selectiontype-enum) \| [`str`](#string-standard) | = | `ALL` | The browser id or selection to get the page ids from. `ALL` Page ids from all open browsers shall be fetched. `ACTIVE` Only page ids from the active browser shall be fetched. |
| `assertion_operator`| : [`AssertionOperator`](#assertionoperator-enum) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` |  |
| `*assertion_expected`| : [`Any`](#any-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) |  |  |  |
| `🏷message`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` |  |

**Return Type**: [`list`](#list-standard)


**Tags**:
- Assertion
- BrowserControl
- Getter

#### Documentation:
Returns a list of page ids based on the context and browser selection. See [Browser, Context and Page](#browser-context-and-page) for more information about Page and related concepts.


`ALL` and `ANY` are synonyms. `ACTIVE` and `CURRENT` are also synonyms.


Example:


```text
Test Case
    `New Page`    https://www.imbus.de
    `New Page`    https://www.reaktor.com
    ${current_page}=   `Get Page IDs`    ACTIVE    ACTIVE    ACTIVE
    Log                Current page ID is: ${current_page}[0]
    ${all_pages}=      `Get Page IDs`    CURRENT   CURRENT   ALL
    Log Many           These are all Page IDs    @{all_pages}
```

Example to count open pages of a specific context:


```text
Test Case
   `New Browser`    firefox
   ${context}=    `New Context`
   `New Page`    https://www.imbus.de
   `New Page`    https://www.op.fi
   `New Context`
   `New Page`    https://www.robocon.io
   ${page_count}=    `Get Page IDs`    ALL    ${context}    ALL    then    len(value)
   Should Be Equal As Integers    ${page_count}    2
```

The ACTIVE page of the ACTIVE context of the ACTIVE Browser is the `Current` Page.


[Comment >>](https://forum.robotframework.org/t//4274)


**In Electron applications:**


The ids are those of the windows of an application and of the `\<webview>` and `WebContentsView` elements they show. [Get Electron Application Catalog](#get-electron-application-catalog) returns them with their titles, and [Get Window Ids](#get-window-ids) returns only the windows.

#### Arguments:

| `assertion_expected`| : [`Any`](#any-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Expected value for the state |
| `message`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | overrides the default error message for assertion. |

**Return Type**: [`Any`](#any-standard)


**Tags**:
- Assertion
- Getter
- PageContent

#### Documentation:
Returns the `property` of the element found by `selector`.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


Optionally asserts that the property value matches the expected value. See [Assertions](#assertions) for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.


If `assertion_operator` is set and the property is not found, `value` is `None` and the keyword does not fail. If no `assertion_operator` is set and the property is not found, the keyword fails. See [Get Attribute](#get-attribute) for examples.


Example:


```text
`Get Property`    h1    innerText    ==    Login Page
${property} =    `Get Property`    h1    innerText
```

If no selector is given the scroll position of the page itself is used (`document.scrollingElement`). See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |
| `key`| : [`AreaFields`](#areafields-enum) | = | `ALL` | Optionally filters the returned values. If keys is set to `ALL` (default) it will return the scroll position as dictionary, otherwise it will just return the single value selected by the key. |

#### Documentation:
Gets elements or pages current scroll position as object `{top: float, left: float, bottom: float, right: float}`.


It describes the rectangle which is visible of the scrollable content of that element. All values are measured from position {top: 0, left: 0}.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


Optionally asserts that the value matches the specified assertion. See [Assertions](#assertions) for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.


See [Get BoundingBox](#get-boundingbox) or [Get Scroll Size](#get-scroll-size) for examples.

Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


Optionally asserts that the state matches the specified assertion. See [Assertions](#assertions) for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.


See [Get BoundingBox](#get-boundingbox) for more similar examples.


Example use:

#### Documentation:
Returns attributes of options of a `select` element as a list of dictionaries.


Each returned dictionary has the keys "index", "value", "label" and "selected".


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


Optionally asserts that these match the specified assertion. See [Assertions](#assertions) for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.


Example:


```text
`Get Select Options`     //select[2]    validate  [v["label"] for v in value] == ["Email", "Mobile"]
`Get Select Options`   select#names     validate  any(v["label"] == "Mikko" for v in value)
```

### Get Selected Options

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Selector from which the info is to be retrieved. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |
| `option_attribute`| : [`SelectAttribute`](#selectattribute-enum) | = | `label` | Which attribute shall be returned/verified. Defaults to label. |
| `assertion_operator`| : [`AssertionOperator`](#assertionoperator-enum) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | See [Assertions](#assertions) for further details. Defaults to None. |
| `*assertion_expected`|   |  |  | Expected value for the state |
| `🏷message`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | overrides the default error message for assertion. |

**Return Type**: [`list`](#list-standard)`[`[`str`](#string-standard) | [`int`](#integer-standard)`]`


**Tags**:
- Assertion
- Getter
- PageContent

#### Documentation:
Returns the specified attribute of selected options of the `select` element.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


Optionally asserts that these match the specified assertion. See [Assertions](#assertions) for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.


- `==` , `!=` and `contains` / `*=` can work with multiple values
- `validate` and `evaluate` only accept one single expected value


Other operators are not allowed.


Example:


```text
`Select Options By`      label                    //select[2]    Email      Mobile
${selected_list} =       `Get Selected Options`   //select[2]                                         # getter
`Get Selected Options`   //select[2]              label          ==         Mobile             Mail   #assertion content
`Select Options By`      label                    select#names   2          4
`Get Selected Options`   select#names             index          ==         2                  4      #assertion index
`Get Selected Options`   select#names             label          *=         Mikko                     #assertion contain
`Get Selected Options`   select#names             label          validate   len(value) == 3           #assertion length
```

### Get Style

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Selector from which the style shall be retrieved. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |
| `key`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `ALL` | Key of the requested CSS property. Retrieves "ALL" styles as dictionary by default. All css settings can be used as keys even if they are not all returned in the dictionary. |
| `assertion_operator`| : [`AssertionOperator`](#assertionoperator-enum) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | See [Assertions](#assertions) for further details. Defaults to None. |
| `assertion_expected`| : [`Any`](#any-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Expected value for the assertion |
| `message`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | overrides the default error message for assertion. |
| `pseudo_element`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Pseudo element to match. Defaults to None. |

**Return Type**: [`dict`](#dictionary-standard)`[`[`str`](#string-standard)`, `[`str`](#string-standard)`]` | [`str`](#string-standard) | [`tuple`](#tuple-standard) | [`dict`](#dictionary-standard)


**Tags**:
- Assertion
- Getter
- PageContent

#### Documentation:
Gets the computed style properties of the element selected by `selector`.


A [pseudo element](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Pseudo-elements) is a CSS functionality to add styles, for example `::before` or `::after`.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


Optionally asserts that the style matches the specified assertion. See [Assertions](#assertions) for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.


When `key` is `ALL`, a dictionary is returned and only the sequence assertion operators `==`, `!=`, `contains` / `*=`, `validate` and `evaluate` / `then` are allowed. Assertion formatters are not applied in that case.

### Get Table Cell Element

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `table`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | selector must select the `\<table>` element that contains both selected elements |
| `column`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | selector can select any `\<th>` or `\<td>` element or one of their descendants. |
| `row`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | selector can select any `\<tr>` element or one of their descendants like `\<td>` elements. |

**Return Type**: [`str`](#string-standard)


**Tags**:
- Getter
- PageContent

#### Documentation:
Returns a selector string for the cell at the same column and row index as the selected elements.


The returned value is used like the one from [Get Element](#get-element).


`column` and `row` can also consume index numbers instead of selectors. Indexes are starting from `0` and `-1` is specific for the last element.


Selectors for `column` and `row` are directly appended to the `table` selector like this: `f"{table} >> {column}"` and `f"{table} >> {row}"`.


| GitHub | Slack | Real Name |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| mkorpela | @mkorpela | Mikko Korpela |
| aaltat | @aaltat | Tatu Aalto |
| xylix | @Kerkko Pelttari | Kerkko Pelttari |
| Snooz82 | @René | René Rohner |


Example:


```text
${table}=    Set Variable    [id="Get Table Cell Element"] >> div.kw-docs table >> nth=1
${e}=    `Get Table Cell Element`    ${table}    "Real Name"    "aaltat"   # Returns element with text ``Tatu Aalto``
Get Text    ${e}    ==    Tatu Aalto
${e}=    `Get Table Cell Element`    ${table}    "Slack"    "Mikko Korpela"   # Returns element with text ``@mkorpela``
Get Text    ${e}    ==    @mkorpela
${e}=    `Get Table Cell Element`    ${table}    "mkorpela"    "Kerkko Pelttari"   # column does not need to be in row 0
Get Text    ${e}    ==    @mkorpela
${e}=    `Get Table Cell Element`    ${table}    2    -1   # Index is also directly possible
Get Text    ${e}    ==    René Rohner
```

[Comment >>](https://forum.robotframework.org/t//4282)

### Get Text

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Selector from which the text is to be retrieved. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |
| `assertion_operator`| : [`AssertionOperator`](#assertionoperator-enum) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | See [Assertions](#assertions) for further details. Defaults to None. |
| `assertion_expected`| : [`Any`](#any-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Expected value for the state |
| `message`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | overrides the default error message for assertion. |
| `🏷text_type`| : [`TextType`](#texttype-enum) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | How text is returned. Possible values are `allInnerTexts`, `allTextContents`, `innerText`, `inputValue`, and `innerHTML`. Defaults to `None`, which returns the value of `input` and `textarea` elements and the inner text of all other elements. |

**Return Type**: [`str`](#string-standard) | [`list`](#list-standard)`[`[`str`](#string-standard)`]` | [`dict`](#dictionary-standard) | [`tuple`](#tuple-standard)


**Tags**:
- Assertion
- Getter
- PageContent

#### Documentation:
Returns text attribute of the element found by `selector`.


Keyword can also return the value property text of `input` or `textarea` elements. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode. The `text_type` argument determines how text is returned. The `allInnerTexts` and `allTextContents` will return a list of strings, while other types return a single string.


Optionally asserts that the text matches the specified assertion. See [Assertions](#assertions) for further details for the assertion arguments. By default, assertion is not done.


Example:


```text
${text} =    `Get Text`    id=important                                # Returns element text without assertion.
${text} =    `Get Text`    id=important    ==    Important text        # Returns element text with assertion.
${text} =    `Get Text`    //input         ==    root                  # Returns input element text with assertion.
${text} =    `Get Text`    id=important    text_type=innerHTML         # Returns element inner HTML.
${text} =    `Get Text`    id=important    text_type=allInnerTexts     # Returns element inner text as list of strings.
```

### Get Viewport Size

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `key`| : [`SizeFields`](#sizefields-enum) | = | `ALL` | Optionally filters the returned values. If keys is set to `ALL` (default) it will return the viewport size as dictionary, otherwise it will just return the single value selected by the key. Note: If a single value is retrieved, an assertion does **not** need a `validate` combined with a cast of `value`. |
| `assertion_operator`| : [`AssertionOperator`](#assertionoperator-enum) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | See [Assertions](#assertions) for further details. Defaults to None. |
| `assertion_expected`| : [`Any`](#any-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Expected value for the assertion |
| `message`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`tuple`](#tuple-standard) \| [`dict`](#dictionary-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | overrides the default error message for assertion. |

**Tags**:
- Assertion
- BrowserControl
- Getter

#### Documentation:
Returns the current viewport dimensions.


Optionally asserts that the state matches the specified assertion. See [Assertions](#assertions) for further details for the assertion arguments. By default assertion is not done.


If the page does not have a viewport size, for example because the context was created without one, `None` is returned and no assertion is done.


Example:


```text
`Get Viewport Size`    ALL    ==    {'width':1280, 'height':720}
`Get Viewport Size`    width    >=    1200
```

[Comment >>](https://forum.robotframework.org/t//4288)


**In Electron applications:**


Returns `None` for the window of an application, which has no emulated viewport. [Get Window Size](#get-window-size) returns the size that the window's page has.

### Get Window Ids

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selection`| : [`SelectionType`](#selectiontype-enum) | = | `ALL` | `ALL` for all windows, in the order in which they opened, `ACTIVE` or `CURRENT` for the window that shows the active page. |

**Return Type**: [`list`](#list-standard)`[`[`str`](#string-standard)`]` — A list of window ids such as `window=1`, which the window keywords take, for example [Maximize Window](#maximize-window) and [Switch Window](#switch-window).


#### Documentation:
Returns the ids of the active application's windows.


The windows are the application's `BrowserWindow` objects. A `\<webview>` or `WebContentsView` is a page, but no window, see [Windows and pages](#windows-and-pages). The ids are valid while the application runs.


Example:


```text
${windows} =    `Get Window Ids`
`Maximize Window`    ${windows}[1]
${active} =    `Get Window Ids`    ACTIVE
```

---

### Get Window Size

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `key`| : [`SizeFields`](#sizefields-enum) | = | `ALL` | `ALL` returns a dictionary with `width` and `height`, `width` or `height` only that value. |
| `assertion_operator`| : [`AssertionOperator`](#assertionoperator-enum) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | See [Assertions](#assertions). |
| `assertion_expected`| : [`Any`](#any-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | The expected value of the assertion. |
| `message`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Overrides the default error message of the assertion. |
| `window`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | The window, see [Windows and pages](#windows-and-pages). Defaults to the window that shows the active page. After the assertion arguments, it is given by name. |

**Return Type**: [`Any`](#any-standard)


#### Documentation:
Returns the content size of a window.


The content size is the area that the window's page shows, see [Set Window Size](#set-window-size). Browser's [Get Viewport Size](#get-viewport-size) returns `None` for an application's window, which has no emulated viewport.


Example:


```text
${size} =    `Get Window Size`
`Get Window Size`    width    ==    1280
`Get Window Size`    ALL    ==    {'width': 1024, 'height': 700}    window=title=Settings
```

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `assertion_operator`| : [`AssertionOperator`](#assertionoperator-enum) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | See [Assertions](#assertions). |
| `assertion_expected`| : [`Any`](#any-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | The expected value of the assertion. |
| `message`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Overrides the default error message of the assertion. |
| `window`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | The window, see [Windows and pages](#windows-and-pages). Defaults to the window that shows the active page. After the assertion arguments, it is given by name. |

**Return Type**: [`Any`](#any-standard)


#### Documentation:
Returns the state of a window: `normal`, `maximized` or `minimized`.


A fullscreen window, which fills the screen, counts as `maximized`.


Example:


```text
`Get Window State`    ==    maximized
${state} =    `Get Window State`    window=title=Settings
```

---

### Get Window Titles


**Return Type**: [`list`](#list-standard)`[`[`str`](#string-standard)`]`


#### Documentation:
Returns the titles that the active application's windows show.


The titles are in the order of [Get Window Ids](#get-window-ids). A window shows the title of its page, unless the application gives it one of its own. The window keywords take a window by its title, see [Windows and pages](#windows-and-pages).


Example:


```text
${titles} =    `Get Window Titles`
Should Contain    ${titles}    Settings
`Switch Window`    title=Settings
```

### Go To

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `url`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | URL to be navigated to. |
| `timeout`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Time to wait for the page to load. If not defined, the library default timeout is used. |
| `wait_until`| : [`PageLoadStates`](#pageloadstates-enum) | = | `load` | When to consider the operation succeeded, defaults to `load`. The event can be either: `domcontentloaded` - consider the operation to be finished when the DOMContentLoaded event is fired. `load` - consider the operation to be finished when the load event is fired. `networkidle` - consider the operation to be finished when there are no network connections for at least 500 ms. `commit` - consider the operation to be finished when the network response is received and the document started loading. |

**Tags**:
- BrowserControl
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Navigates to the given `url`.


Returns the HTTP status code of the navigation request as an integer, or 0 if no response was received.


If the wait times out, the page's load report is logged: whether its navigation committed, how far the document got and which requests were still open.

### Handle Future Dialogs

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `action`| : [`DialogAction`](#dialogaction-enum) |  |  | How to handle the alert. Can be `accept` or `dismiss`. |
| `prompt_input`| : [`str`](#string-standard) | = | `${EMPTY}` | The value to enter into the prompt. Only valid if the `action` argument equals `accept`. Defaults to an empty string. |

**Tags**:
- PageContent

#### Documentation:
Handle next dialog on page with `action`.


The dialog can be an alert, beforeunload, confirm or prompt dialog. This keyword must be called before the action, for example a click, which triggers the dialog.


The handler is registered on the current page and stays in effect for all following dialogs on that page. Calling this keyword again on the same page replaces the handler, so the latest call decides how dialogs are handled.


If a handler is not set, dialogs are dismissed by default.


The handler runs when the dialog appears, not while this keyword executes, so a failure to accept or dismiss the dialog can not be raised as a keyword failure. Such a failure is reported in the playwright-log.txt file only, which is linked into the Robot Framework log when a keyword fails.


Example:


```text
`Handle Future Dialogs`    action=accept
`Click`                    \#alerts
```

[Comment >>](https://forum.robotframework.org/t//4293)


**In Electron applications:**


Electron does not implement `prompt()`: a page's call fails with `prompt() is not supported.`, so `prompt_input` never applies. Native dialogs of the main process are not dialogs of the page; replace them with [Evaluate In Main Process](#evaluate-in-main-process).

### Highlight Elements

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Selectors which shall be highlighted. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |
| `duration`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) | = | `0:00:05` | Sets for how long the selector shall be highlighted. Defaults to `5s` => 5 seconds. If set to 0 seconds, the highlighting is not deleted. |
| `width`| : [`str`](#string-standard) | = | `2px` | Sets the width of the highlight border. Defaults to 2px. |
| `style`| : [`str`](#string-standard) | = | `dotted` | Sets the style of the border. Defaults to dotted. |
| `color`| : [`str`](#string-standard) | = | `blue` | Sets the color of the border. Valid colors i.e. are: `red`, `blue`, `yellow`, `pink`, `black` |
| `🏷mode`| : [`HighlightMode`](#highlightmode-enum) | = | `border` | Sets the mode of the highlight. Valid modes are: `border` (classic mode), `playwright` (Playwright's native one) and `both`. Defaults to `border`. If `playwright` is used, `width`, `style` and `color` are ignored and only one highlighting can happen at the same time. |

**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Adds a highlight to elements matched by the `selector`. Provides a style adjustment.


Returns the number of highlighted elements. Keyword does not fail, if the `selector` matched zero elements in the page. Keyword does not scroll elements to viewport and highlighted element might be outside the viewport. Use [Scroll To Element](#scroll-to-element) keyword to scroll element in viewport.


Keyword does not fail if selector resolves to multiple elements.


Highlights which are created with `duration=0` stay in the page until they are removed. Calling this keyword with an empty `selector`, for example `Highlight Elements    ${EMPTY}`, removes all such highlights that were made with Playwright's native highlighting, in other words with `mode=playwright` or `mode=both`. Highlights drawn in `border` mode can not be removed that way.


Example:


```text
`Highlight Elements`    input#login_button    duration=200ms
${count} =    `Highlight Elements`    input#login_button    duration=200ms    width=4px    style=solid    color=\#FF00FF
Should Be Equal    ${count}    ${5}
```

### Hover

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Selector element to hover. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |
| `position_x`| : [`float`](#float-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | A point to hover relative to the top-left corner of element bounding box. If not specified, hovers over some visible point of the element. Only positive values within the bounding-box are allowed. Both values must be given, otherwise the position is ignored. |
| `position_y`| : [`float`](#float-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | A point to hover relative to the top-left corner of element bounding box. If not specified, hovers over some visible point of the element. Only positive values within the bounding-box are allowed. Both values must be given, otherwise the position is ignored. |
| `force`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | Set to `True` to skip Playwright's [Actionability checks](https://playwright.dev/docs/actionability). Defaults to `False`. |
| `*modifiers`| : [`KeyboardModifier`](#keyboardmodifier-enum) |  |  | Modifier keys to press. Ensures that only these modifiers are pressed during the hover, and then restores current modifiers back. If not specified, currently pressed modifiers are used. Valid modifier keys are `Alt`, `Control`, `ControlOrMeta`, `Meta` and `Shift`. |

**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Moves the virtual mouse and scrolls to the element found by `selector`.


This method hovers over an element matching `selector` by performing the following steps:


- Find an element matching `selector`. If there is none, wait until a matching element is attached to the DOM.
- Wait for actionability checks on the matched element, unless the `force` option is set. If the element is detached during the checks, the whole action is retried.
- Scroll the element into view if needed.
- Use [Mouse Move](#mouse-move) to hover over the center of the element, or the specified `position`.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


Example:


```text
`Hover`    h1
`Hover`    h1    10   20    Alt
```

### Http

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `url`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | The request url, e.g. `/api/foo`. |
| `method`| : [`RequestMethod`](#requestmethod-enum) | = | `GET` | The HTTP method for the request. Defaults to GET. |
| `body`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | The request body. It is ignored for GET requests, because GET requests cannot have a body. If the body can be parsed as JSON, the `Content-Type` header for the request is automatically set to `application/json`, unless `headers` already contains that header. Defaults to None. |
| `headers`| : [`dict`](#dictionary-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | A dictionary of additional request headers. Defaults to None. |

**Return Type**: [`Any`](#any-standard)


**Tags**:
- HTTP

#### Documentation:
Performs an HTTP request in the current browser context


The request is sent with the browser's `fetch` from the currently active page, so a relative `url` is resolved against the URL of that page.


The response is a Robot Framework dictionary with the following attributes:


- `status` \<int> The status code of the response.
- `statusText` \<str> Status text corresponding to `status`, e.g. OK or INTERNAL SERVER ERROR. This may not be available for all browsers.
- `body` \<dict> | \<str> The response body. If the body can be parsed as a JSON object, it will be returned as Python dictionary, otherwise it is returned as a string.
- `headers` \<dict> A dictionary containing all response headers.
- `ok` \<bool> Whether the request was successful, i.e. the `status` is in the range 200-299.
- `url` \<str> The final URL of the response, after possible redirects.
- `redirected` \<bool> Whether the response is the result of a redirect.
- `type` \<str> The type of the response, e.g. `basic` or `cors`.


Here's an example of using Robot Framework dictionary variables and extended variable syntax to do assertions on the response object:


```text
&{res}=             `HTTP`                       /api/endpoint
Should Be Equal     ${res.status}              200
Should Be Equal     ${res.body.some_field}     some value
```

### Install Credential


**Tags**:
- Credential
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Installs the virtual WebAuthn authenticator into the context.


Overrides `navigator.credentials.create()` and `navigator.credentials.get()` in all current and future pages of the context. Call this before the page first touches `navigator.credentials`.


Until the authenticator is installed, no interception is in place and the page sees the platform's native (or absent) WebAuthn behavior. [Create Credential](#create-credential) installs the authenticator as well, so this keyword is mainly needed when the credentials are created by the application itself. There must be an open context, otherwise the keyword fails.


Example:


```text
`New Context`
`Install Credential`
`New Page`    ${SUT_URL}
# Do something on the page that causes the page to call ``navigator.credentials.create()``
${credential_id} =    Get Credential Id   # This is a user keyword that returns the credential id from somewhere. Talk to your application team to find out how to get the credential id.
${credential} =    `Get Credential`    id_=${credential_id}    # This will return the credential that was created by the application and installed into the context.
`New Context`
`Create Credential`
...    rpId=${DOMAIN_NAME}
...    id_=${credential["id"]}
...    privateKey=${credential["privateKey"]}
...    publicKey=${credential["publicKey"]}
...    userHandle=${credential["userHandle"]}
`New Page`    ${SUT_URL}
# User should be able to interact with the page using the installed credential.
```

### Keyboard Key

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `action`| : [`KeyAction`](#keyaction-enum) |  |  | Determines whether the key should be released (`up`), held down (`down`) or pressed once (`press`). `down` and `up` are useful for combinations, i.e. with Shift. |
| `key`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | The key to be pressed. Examples of valid keys are: `F1` - `F12`, `Digit0` - `Digit9`, `KeyA` - `KeyZ`, `Backquote`, `Minus`, `Equal`, `Backslash`, `Backspace`, `Tab`, `Delete`, `Escape`, `ArrowDown`, `End`, `Enter`, `Home`, `Insert`, `PageDown`, `PageUp`, `ArrowRight`, `ArrowUp` , etc. |
| `🏷delay`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) | = | `0:00:00` | Time the key is held down between keydown and keyup, in Robot Framework's time format. Only valid with action `press`, other actions raise an error. Defaults to `0 s`. Example: `50 ms` |

**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Press a keyboard key on the virtual keyboard or set a key up or down.


Useful keys for `down` and `up` for example are: `Shift`, `Control`, `Alt`, `Meta`, `ShiftLeft`


Example execution:


```text
`Keyboard Key`    press    S
`Keyboard Key`    press    S        delay=500 ms
`Keyboard Key`    down     Shift
`Keyboard Key`    press    ArrowLeft
`Keyboard Key`    press    Delete
`Keyboard Key`    up       Shift
```

Note: Capital letters don't need to be written by the help of Shift. You can type them in directly.


[Comment >>](https://forum.robotframework.org/t//4298)


**In Electron applications:**


The keys reach the page, but not the accelerators of the application's menu. Click a menu item in the main process instead, see [Evaluate In Main Process](#evaluate-in-main-process).

### Merge Coverage Reports

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `input_folder`| : [`Path`](#path-standard) |  |  | Path to the base folder where the raw coverage reports are located. |
| `output_folder`| : [`Path`](#path-standard) |  |  | Path to the folder where the combined report is stored. |
| `config_file`| : [`Path`](#path-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Optional path to [options file](https://www.npmjs.com/package/monocart-coverage-reports#options) |
| `name`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Optional name for the combined report. |
| `reports`| : [`list`](#list-standard)`[`[`str`](#string-standard)`]` \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Optional list of reporters to create. Default is `v8`. |

**Return Type**: [`Path`](#path-standard)


**Tags**:
- Coverage
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Combines multiple raw coverage reports into a single report.


Returns the path to the `output_folder`.


The `input_folder` argument is the base folder where the coverage reports are located. The keyword will look into each subfolder and if the subfolder contains a "raw" folder, it will use the data from the "raw" folder for the combined report.


The `output_folder` argument is the folder where the combined report is saved. If the folder does not exist, it is created. If the folder exists, its content is deleted before the report is created.


The `output_folder` and `input_folder` must be full paths to the folders.


The `config_file` argument is optional and can be used to provide a path to a monocart-coverage-reports options file. If the file is defined but does not exist, the keyword fails. For more details see: [https://www.npmjs.com/package/monocart-coverage-reports\#config-file](https://www.npmjs.com/package/monocart-coverage-reports#config-file)


The `name` argument is optional and can be used to provide a name for the combined report. If it is not defined, the report is named "Browser library Merged Coverage Report".


The `reports` argument is optional and can be used to provide a list of reporters to create. Default is `v8`.


The keyword combines only the raw reports. To get raw reports, the [Start Coverage](#start-coverage) keyword must be called with the `raw=True` argument. If no raw reports are found from the `input_folder`, the keyword fails. The keyword should be used when there is a need to combine multiple reports into a single report. For example, when tests are run in multiple pages. The example below demonstrates how to use the keyword.


Example:


```text
`New Page`
`Start Coverage`
`Go To`    ${LOGIN_URL}
Test Feature X In The Page
`Stop Coverage`
`New Page`
`Start Coverage`
`Go To`    ${LOGIN_URL}
Test Feature Y In The Page
`Stop Coverage`
`Merge Coverage Reports`    ${OUTPUT_DIR}/browser/coverage    ${OUTPUT_DIR}/browser/combined-coverage
```

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `window`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | The window, see [Windows and pages](#windows-and-pages). Defaults to the window that shows the active page. |

**Return Type**: [`None`](#none-standard)


#### Documentation:
Minimises a window and waits until it is minimised.


A minimised window draws nothing, so Browser keywords on its page wait until their timeout. [Restore Window](#restore-window) brings it back. A fullscreen window leaves fullscreen first. Minimising needs a window manager, and some desktops cannot minimise windows, for example niri. There, the keyword fails after the library timeout.

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|

| `x`| : [`float`](#float-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Coordinates to move to before the action is executed. Both must be given, otherwise the action happens at the current mouse position. |
| `y`| : [`float`](#float-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Coordinates to move to before the action is executed. Both must be given, otherwise the action happens at the current mouse position. |
| `button`| : [`MouseButton`](#mousebutton-enum) | = | `left` | One of `left`, `middle` or `right`. Defaults to `left`. |
| `clickCount`| : [`int`](#integer-standard) | = | `${1}` | Determines how often the button shall be clicked if action is equal to `click`. Defaults to 1. |
| `delay`| : [`int`](#integer-standard) \| [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) | = | `0:00:00` | Delay in Robot Framework time format between the mousedown and mouseup event. Can only be set if the action is `click`. Defaults to `0 s`. |

**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Clicks, presses or releases a mouse button.


**Attention:** Argument type `int` for 'delay' in milliseconds has been changed to [timedelta](#timedelta-standard) in Browser 14.0.0. Use Robot Framework time format instead. For refactoring just add 'ms' after the delay number.


Delay Example:


```text
`Mouse Button`    click    delay=100 ms
`Mouse Button`    click    delay=${dyn_delay} ms
```

Moving the mouse between holding down and releasing it is possible with [Mouse Move](#mouse-move).


Example:


```text
`Hover`                     "Obstacle"           # Move mouse over the element
`Mouse Button`              down                 # Press mouse button down
`Mouse Move Relative To`    "Obstacle"    500    # Drag mouse
`Mouse Button`              up                   # Release mouse button
```

#### Arguments:

| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Identifies the element whose center is the start-point. |
| `x`| : [`float`](#float-standard) | = | `${0.0}` | Coordinates relative to the center of the element's bounding box. |

| `steps`| : [`int`](#integer-standard) | = | `${1}` | Number of intermediate steps for the mouse event. Often it is necessary to send more than one intermediate event to get the desired result. Defaults to 1. |

**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Moves the mouse cursor relative to the selected element.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


Example:

```text
`Mouse Move Relative To`    id=indicator    -100
```

### Pause At

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `time`| : [`datetime`](#datetime-standard) |  |  | The time to pause the clock at. |

**Tags**:
- Clock
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Advances the clock by jumping forward in time and pauses it.


Fires due timers at most once. This is equivalent to a user closing the laptop lid for a while and reopening it at the specified time and then pausing. Pause can not move the clock backwards.


Example:


```text
`Set Time`         2024-10-31 17:34:00    # Set the clock to a specific time
Do Something                            # Implement this in your keyword
`Pause At`         2024-10-31 18:34:00    # Pause the clock at a specific time
Check Something                         # Also this is implemented in your keyword
`Resume Clock`                            # Resume the clock
Do Something Else                       # Do something after clock runs normally
```

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Selector of the text field. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |
| `*keys`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Keys to be pressed one after the other. Combining modifiers with a single key press by chaining them with `+`, like `Control+Shift+T`, is supported. |
| `🏷press_duration`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) | = | `0:00:00` | Delay between keydown and keyup of each key. Can be given as seconds (float) or as Robot Framework time string. Defaults to `0 ms`. Example: `50 ms` |
| `🏷key_delay`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) | = | `0:00:00` | Delay between key presses. Can be given as seconds (float) or as Robot Framework time string. Defaults to `0 ms`. Example: `50 ms` |

**Tags**:

#### Documentation:
Types the given key combination into element found by `selector`.


Supports values like `a` or `b` which will be automatically typed.


Also supports identifiers for keys like `ArrowLeft` or `Backspace`.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


See Playwright's documentation for a more comprehensive list of supported input keys. [Playwright docs for press.](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-press)


Example:


```text
# Keyword         Selector                    *Keys
`Press Keys`      //*[@id="username_field"]    h    e   l   o   ArrowLeft   l
```

### Promise To

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `kw`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Keyword that will run asynchronously in the background. |
| `*args`|   |  |  | Keyword arguments as normally used. |

**Return Type**: `Future`


**Tags**:
- Wait

#### Documentation:
Wrap a Browser library keyword and make it a promise.


The promised keyword is started in the background. Test execution continues without waiting for `kw` to finish.


Returns a reference to the promised keyword. Use [Wait For](#wait-for) or [Wait For All Promises](#wait-for-all-promises) to wait for its result. Promises that are never waited for are waited for automatically at the end of the test, and a warning is logged.


Only Browser library keywords can be promised, any other keyword name fails the keyword.


Example:


```text
${promise}=     `Promise To`            Wait For Response     matcher=     timeout=3
`Click`           \#delayed_request
${body}=        `Wait For`              ${promise}
```

### Promise To Upload File

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `path`| : [`PathLike`](#path-standard) |  |  | Path to file to be uploaded. |

**Return Type**: `Future`


**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Returns a promise that resolves when the file from `path` has been uploaded.


The file from `path` is uploaded into the next file chooser dialog on the page.


The keyword fails immediately if `path` does not point to an existing file. The promise fails if no file chooser dialog is opened within the timeout.


Example use:


```text
${promise}=    `Promise To Upload File`    ${CURDIR}/test_upload_file.txt
`Click`          id=open_file_chooser_button
${upload_result}=    `Wait For`    ${promise}
```

Alternatively, you can use the [Upload File By Selector](#upload-file-by-selector) keyword.

### Promise To Wait For Download

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `saveAs`| : [`str`](#string-standard) | = | `${EMPTY}` | Defines path where the file is saved persistently. File will also temporarily be saved in playwright context's default download location. If empty, generated unique path (GUID) is used and file is deleted when the context is closed. |
| `wait_for_finished`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${True}` | If true, promise will wait for download to finish. If false, promise will resolve immediately after download has started. |
| `download_timeout`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Maximum total time for the download to start and finish, counted from the moment the promise is created. If the download does not start within this time, the keyword fails. If it starts but does not finish, it is cancelled and the keyword fails. If `wait_for_finished` is `False`, only the start is limited. If not set, the download must start within the browser timeout, see [Set Browser Timeout](#set-browser-timeout), and there is no limit for it to finish. |

**Return Type**: `Future`


**Tags**:
- BrowserControl
- Wait

#### Documentation:
Returns a promise that waits for the next download event on the page.


To enable downloads the context's `acceptDownloads` needs to be true.


With the default file path downloaded files are deleted when the context the download happened in is closed.


If browser is connected remotely with `Connect To Browser` then `saveAs` must be set to store it locally where the browser runs!


Keyword returns dictionary of type [DownloadInfo](#downloadinfo-typeddict) which contains downloaded file path and suggested filename as well as state and downloadID. Example:


```text
{
  "saveAs": "/tmp/robotframework-browser/downloads/2f1b3b7c-1b1b-4b1b-9b1b-1b1b1b1b1b1b",
  "suggestedFilename": "downloaded_file.txt",
  "state": "finished",
  "downloadID": None
}
```

If `wait_for_finished` is `False`, `saveAs` is an empty string, `state` is `in_progress` and `downloadID` contains an id which can be used with [Get Download State](#get-download-state) to check the download later.


The keyword `New Browser` has a `downloadsPath` setting which can be used to set the default download directory. If `saveAs` is set to a relative path, the file will be saved relative to the browser's `downloadsPath` setting or if that is not set, relative to the Playwright's working directory. If `saveAs` is set to an absolute path, the file will be saved to that absolute path independent of `downloadsPath`.


Set `download_timeout` when the download can take longer than the browser timeout, for example when the server generates the file before sending it.


If the URL for the file to download shall be used, [Download](#download) keyword may be a simpler alternative way to download the file.


The waited promise returns a dictionary which contains saveAs and suggestedFilename as keys. The saveAs contains the location where the file is downloaded and suggestedFilename contains the suggested name for the download. The suggestedFilename is typically computed by the browser from the Content-Disposition response header or the download attribute. See the spec on [whatwg](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#downloading-resources). Different browsers can use different logic for computing it.


Example usage:


```text
`New Context`            acceptDownloads=True
`New Page`               ${LOGIN_URL}
${dl_promise}          `Promise To Wait For Download`    /path/to/download/file.name    download_timeout=30s
`Click`                  id=file_download
${file_obj}=           `Wait For`    ${dl_promise}
File Should Exist      ${file_obj}[saveAs]
Should Be True         ${file_obj.suggestedFilename}
```

### Record Keyword

#### Arguments:

| | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `name`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  |
| `file`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `\${SUITE_SOURCE}` |
| `idle_timeout`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `0:05:00` |

**Return Type**: [`str`](#string-standard)


**Tags**:
- Recorder

#### Documentation:
Record browser interactions as one User Keyword named `name`.


Shows the Robot Framework recorder toolbar on the pages of the **current** browser context and blocks until the recording ends. Every Action becomes a Keyword Call to a Browser keyword, is listed in the toolbar and is written to `file` immediately.


Toolbar buttons (each has a tooltip):


- **✕** in the header: ends the session.
- **Minimize** in the header (a dash): minimizes the toolbar.
- **Discard**: drops the Keyword Calls recorded so far and starts the keyword again, empty.
- **Undo**: removes the Keyword Calls of the last Action.
- **Pause** (two bars): stops recording until **Resume**; Actions in between are not recorded.
- **Pick** in the header: picks an element on the page, as [Record Selector](#record-selector) does, and adds its selector to the keyword as a comment row `\# Picked Selector    \<selector>`. Playwright's own Pick locator button opens the same picker. While picking, nothing is recorded; **Cancel** returns to recording without a row.


The toolbar is in the recording state from the start. Click a value or a selector in the toolbar to turn the whole of it, or a marked part, into a Keyword Argument, named like `email` or `${email}`. The same dialog asks whether the marked value becomes the argument's default. The toolbar also offers to use the new argument for the same value elsewhere in the keyword (replacing repeated values).


The keyword is always created new: an existing keyword is never extended.


The recording ends with **Save** or **✕** in the toolbar, with Playwright's Record button, when `idle_timeout` passes without any Action or toolbar command, when all pages are closed, or on an error. The keyword being recorded is saved unless it has no Keyword Calls.


| Arguments | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `name` | Name of the User Keyword to create. It must not exist in `file` and must not shadow any keyword the running suite can call. |
| `file` | Target `.robot` or `.resource` file. Defaults to `${SUITE_SOURCE}`, the file of the running suite; in a suite initialisation file that is its `__init__.robot`, and a keyword recorded there can only be used in that file. A relative path is resolved against the current working directory, not against the suite; use `${CURDIR}` for a file next to the suite. The folder must exist and an existing file must be writable; both are checked before recording starts. With `${None}` nothing is written; the keyword is logged to the console and to the log at INFO level instead. |
| `idle_timeout` | Ends the recording after this long without an Action or toolbar command. Must be greater than zero. Default: 5 minutes, so a forgotten recording does not block the run for good. `${None}` waits without limit. |


Returns the text of the recorded keyword, including the `*** Keywords ***` header. If a recorded keyword cannot be written - the file became read-only, the disk is full - the keyword fails, and the recorded text is logged as a warning so nothing is lost.


What is generated: every keyword gets `[Tags]    recorded`. A popup or new tab becomes `Switch Page    NEW`. An Action on another open page gets a `Switch Page` to it first, using the id the Switch Page that left that page returned (`${page}=    Switch Page    NEW`); a page closed by hand becomes `Close Page`, or `Close Page    ${page}` when it is not the active one. A page the keyword has no id of, for example one open before the recording, cannot be switched to, and the toolbar says so. A dialog gets `Handle Future Dialogs    action=accept` before the Action (Playwright does not report whether the dialog was accepted); a download is wrapped in `Promise To Wait For Download` and `Wait For`. A file chosen in a file chooser wraps the click that opened it in `Promise To Upload File` and `Wait For`; the page never reveals the file's folder, so the path reads `\<define_path_to_file>/\<file name>` and must be completed (or made an argument). Playwright's Assert snapshot becomes `Get Aria Snapshot` with an exact YAML comparison, and Assert visibility becomes `Get Element States    ...    *=    visible`. Playwright folds a navigation that happens within 5 seconds after a click, fill or key press into that Action, so it is not recorded as a `Go To` of its own. Hovers are not recorded, because Playwright does not report them. Other Actions without a Browser keyword are only reported in the toolbar.


Needs a visible browser: fails if the active browser was opened headless, since nobody could use the toolbar there. A browser attached with `Connect To Browser` is assumed to be visible.


Limitations: only the **current** browser context is recorded; other contexts are ignored. Playwright's own recorder toolbar is shown at the top centre of the page during the recording and cannot be hidden, so it covers the page there. The toolbar does not appear on a page whose Content-Security-Policy allows only Trusted Types policies it names, nor in a document without a body, such as an SVG file. A modal `\<dialog>` of the page covers the toolbar until it is closed, and a click there is recorded on the dialog.


**Review a recorded keyword before you commit it.** Its values come from the page under test, including anything typed into password fields. During the session the toolbar state, including the recorded values and typed text, is readable by scripts of every page in the context, and those scripts can send toolbar commands. Keystrokes typed into the toolbar do not reach the page, except to a `window` capture listener the page registered before the toolbar was injected.


Requires a Playwright version that offers the programmatic recorder. The context stays prepared for recording after the session ends.


Example:


```text
${text} =    Record Keyword    Login As Admin
Record Keyword    Search Product    ${CURDIR}/shop.resource    idle_timeout=15 min
Record Keyword    Try Something    file=${None}
```

See [Record Keywords](#record-keywords) to record several keywords in one session.

---

### Record Keywords

#### Arguments:

| | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `file`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `\${SUITE_SOURCE}` |
| `idle_timeout`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `0:05:00` |

**Return Type**: [`str`](#string-standard)


**Tags**:
- Recorder

#### Documentation:
Record several User Keywords in one session.


Use **Record keyword** in the toolbar to name and start a keyword, record it, and **Save** it; then start the next one. Actions while no keyword is being recorded are not captured, so you can navigate freely between keywords. A name must not exist in `file`, must not have been recorded earlier in the session, and must not shadow any keyword the running suite can call - such names are rejected in the toolbar.


Shows the Robot Framework recorder toolbar on the pages of the **current** browser context and blocks until the recording ends. Every Action becomes a Keyword Call to a Browser keyword, is listed in the toolbar and is written to `file` immediately.


Toolbar buttons (each has a tooltip):


- **✕** in the header: ends the session.
- **Minimize** in the header (a dash): minimizes the toolbar.
- **Record keyword**: names and starts a keyword.
- **Discard**: drops the keyword being recorded, also from `file`, and returns to idle.
- **Undo**: removes the Keyword Calls of the last Action.
- **Pause** (two bars): stops recording until **Resume**; Actions in between are not recorded.
- **Pick** in the header: picks an element on the page, as [Record Selector](#record-selector) does, and adds its selector to the keyword as a comment row `\# Picked Selector    \<selector>`. Playwright's own Pick locator button opens the same picker. While picking, nothing is recorded; **Cancel** returns to recording without a row.
- **Save**: saves the keyword being recorded and returns to idle.


While the toolbar is minimized, its header offers **Start** (idle) or **Save** (recording).


The toolbar is idle until a keyword is started; Actions while idle are not recorded. While recording, click a value or a selector in the toolbar to turn the whole of it, or a marked part, into a Keyword Argument, named like `email` or `${email}`. The same dialog asks whether the marked value becomes the argument's default. The toolbar also offers to use the new argument for the same value elsewhere in the keyword (replacing repeated values).


Existing keywords are never extended.


The recording ends with **✕** in the toolbar header, with Playwright's Record button, when `idle_timeout` passes without any Action or toolbar command, when all pages are closed, or on an error. The keyword being recorded is saved unless it has no Keyword Calls.


| Arguments | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `file` | Target `.robot` or `.resource` file. Defaults to `${SUITE_SOURCE}`, the file of the running suite; in a suite initialisation file that is its `__init__.robot`, and a keyword recorded there can only be used in that file. A relative path is resolved against the current working directory, not against the suite; use `${CURDIR}` for a file next to the suite. The folder must exist and an existing file must be writable; both are checked before recording starts. With `${None}` nothing is written; the keywords are logged to the console and to the log at INFO level instead. |
| `idle_timeout` | Ends the recording after this long without an Action or toolbar command. Must be greater than zero. Default: 5 minutes, so a forgotten recording does not block the run for good. `${None}` waits without limit. |


Returns the text of all keywords recorded in the session, under one `*** Keywords ***` header. If a recorded keyword cannot be written - the file became read-only, the disk is full - the keyword fails, and the recorded text is logged as a warning so nothing is lost.


What is generated: every keyword gets `[Tags]    recorded`. A popup or new tab becomes `Switch Page    NEW`. An Action on another open page gets a `Switch Page` to it first, using the id the Switch Page that left that page returned (`${page}=    Switch Page    NEW`); a page closed by hand becomes `Close Page`, or `Close Page    ${page}` when it is not the active one. A page the keyword has no id of, for example one open before the recording, cannot be switched to, and the toolbar says so. A dialog gets `Handle Future Dialogs    action=accept` before the Action (Playwright does not report whether the dialog was accepted); a download is wrapped in `Promise To Wait For Download` and `Wait For`. A file chosen in a file chooser wraps the click that opened it in `Promise To Upload File` and `Wait For`; the page never reveals the file's folder, so the path reads `\<define_path_to_file>/\<file name>` and must be completed (or made an argument). Playwright's Assert snapshot becomes `Get Aria Snapshot` with an exact YAML comparison, and Assert visibility becomes `Get Element States    ...    *=    visible`. Playwright folds a navigation that happens within 5 seconds after a click, fill or key press into that Action, so it is not recorded as a `Go To` of its own. Hovers are not recorded, because Playwright does not report them. Other Actions without a Browser keyword are only reported in the toolbar.


Needs a visible browser: fails if the active browser was opened headless, since nobody could use the toolbar there. A browser attached with `Connect To Browser` is assumed to be visible.


Limitations: only the **current** browser context is recorded; other contexts are ignored. Playwright's own recorder toolbar is shown at the top centre of the page during the recording and cannot be hidden, so it covers the page there. The toolbar does not appear on a page whose Content-Security-Policy allows only Trusted Types policies it names, nor in a document without a body, such as an SVG file. A modal `\<dialog>` of the page covers the toolbar until it is closed, and a click there is recorded on the dialog.


**Review recorded keywords before you commit them.** Their values come from the page under test, including anything typed into password fields. During the session the toolbar state, including the recorded values and typed text, is readable by scripts of every page in the context, and those scripts can send toolbar commands. Keystrokes typed into the toolbar do not reach the page, except to a `window` capture listener the page registered before the toolbar was injected.


Requires a Playwright version that offers the programmatic recorder. The context stays prepared for recording after the session ends.


Example:


```text
${text} =    Record Keywords
Record Keywords    ${CURDIR}/resources/shop.resource    idle_timeout=${None}
```

See [Record Keyword](#record-keyword) to record exactly one keyword.

### Record Selector

#### Arguments:

| | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `label`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` |
| `generator`| : [`SelectorGenerator`](#selectorgenerator-enum) | = | `playwright` |
| `idle_timeout`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `0:05:00` |

**Return Type**: [`str`](#string-standard)


**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Recorder

#### Documentation:
Pick an element on the active page and return a selector for it.


Shows the Robot Framework toolbar on the active page and blocks until a selector is chosen. Move the pointer over the page: Playwright highlights the element under it and names it in a tooltip. Click to pick it; the click does not reach the page. Elements inside frames and open shadow roots can be picked too.


The toolbar then shows the selector for the picked element:


- **Playwright** / **CSS**: switches between the selector generators for the same element, see [SelectorGenerator](#selectorgenerator-enum).
- The selector itself can be edited. The elements it finds stay highlighted on the page, and the toolbar counts them; after an edit both follow once typing pauses for a second. One match is what most keywords need, several are shown as a warning, none as an error. The highlight ends with the keyword.
- **Highlight** (a dashed square): switches the highlight off and on; it is on by default.
- **Reselect**: picks another element.
- **Use**: returns the selector, also when it does not find exactly one element.
- **✕** in the header, or Escape in the toolbar: cancels, and the keyword fails.
- Minimized, the header offers **Reselect** and **Use** once an element is picked.


| Arguments | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `label` | Shown in the toolbar header, to say which element to pick. |
| `generator` | The generator the toolbar starts with; the toolbar can switch it. `playwright` (default) or `css`. |
| `idle_timeout` | Fails the keyword after this long without a pick or toolbar command. Must be greater than zero. Default: 5 minutes. `${None}` waits without limit. |


Fails in a headless browser, while a [Record Keyword](#record-keyword) or [Record Keywords](#record-keywords) session runs in the browser context, when the page is closed, on cancel and when the `idle_timeout` passes.


The toolbar has the limits of the [Record Keyword](#record-keyword) toolbar: it does not appear on a page whose Content-Security-Policy allows only Trusted Types policies it names, nor in a document without a body.


Like the recorder toolbar, the toolbar's commands are reachable by scripts of the page under test: use it on applications you trust, and check the selector you get.


Example:


```text
${selector} =    `Record Selector`    Login button
`Click`    ${selector}
${heading} =    `Record Selector`    Page header    generator=css
`Get Text`    ${heading}    ==    Expected text
```

### Register Keyword To Run On Failure

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `keyword`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) |  |  | The name of a keyword that will be executed if a Browser keyword fails. It is possible to use any available keyword, including user keywords or keywords from other libraries. |
| `*args`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | The arguments to the keyword if any. |
| `🏷scope`| : [`Scope`](#scope-enum) | = | `Global` | Scope defines the lifetime of this setting. Available values are `Global`, `Suite` or `Test` / `Task`. See [Scope Setting](#scope-setting) for more details. |

**Return Type**: `DelayedKeyword`


**Tags**:
- Config

#### Documentation:
Sets the keyword to execute, when a Browser keyword fails.


The initial keyword to use is set when [importing](#importing) the library, and the keyword that is used by default is `Take Screenshot  fail-screenshot-{index}`. Taking a screenshot when something failed is a very useful feature, but notice that it can slow down the execution.


It is possible to use string `NONE` or any other robot falsy name, case-insensitively, as well as Python `None` to disable this feature altogether.


This keyword returns an object which contains the previously registered failure keyword. The return value can always be used to restore the original value later. The returned object contains the keyword name and the possible arguments used for the keyword.


If the [Take Screenshot](#take-screenshot) keyword is registered as run on failure keyword without positional arguments and without the `filename` argument, then the default value of the `filename` argument is not used as screenshot file name. Instead, `${TEST NAME}_FAILURE_SCREENSHOT_{index}` in the output directory is used as file name. If there is a need to use the default value of the `filename` argument, use `robotframework-browser-screenshot-{index}` as the `filename` argument value.


Example:


```text
`Register Keyword To Run On Failure`    Take Screenshot    # Uses ${TEST NAME}_FAILURE_SCREENSHOT_{index} as filename
`Register Keyword To Run On Failure`    Take Screenshot    robotframework-browser-screenshot-{index}    # Uses robotframework-browser-screenshot-{index} as filename
${previous kw}=    `Register Keyword To Run On Failure`    NONE    # Disables run on failure functionality.
`Register Keyword To Run On Failure`    ${previous kw}
`Register Keyword To Run On Failure`    Take Screenshot    fullPage=True
`Register Keyword To Run On Failure`    Take Screenshot    failure-{index}    fullPage=True
```

[Comment >>](https://forum.robotframework.org/t//4316)

### Reload

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `timeout`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Maximum time for the reload to succeed. If not given, the currently set browser timeout is used. |
| `waitUntil`| : [`PageLoadStates`](#pageloadstates-enum) | = | `load` | When to consider the operation succeeded, defaults to `load`. |

**Tags**:
- BrowserControl
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Reloads current active page.


`waitUntil` events can be either: `domcontentloaded` - consider the operation to be finished when the DOMContentLoaded event is fired. `load` - consider the operation to be finished when the load event is fired. `networkidle` - consider the operation to be finished when there are no network connections for at least 500 ms. `commit` - consider the operation to be finished when the network response is received and the document started loading.


If the wait times out, the page's load report is logged: whether its navigation committed, how far the document got and which requests were still open.

### Remove Locator Handler

#### Arguments:

| | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `locator`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  |

**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Remove the locator handler indicated by `locator`.


The `locator` must be exactly the same string that was used as the `selector` argument when the handler was added. Handlers are tied to the page in which they were added, therefore this keyword removes the handler from the active page only. If no handler is found, the keyword does not fail, it only logs that no handler was found.

### Save Storage State

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `path`| : [`Path`](#path-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Where the state file is written. Relative paths are resolved against the current working directory and missing parent directories are created. If the file already exists, it is overwritten. If not given, a file with a generated name is created in `${OUTPUTDIR}`/browser/state. The absolute path of the written file is returned. |
| `🏷indexedDB`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | Also save IndexedDB. Needed by applications, like Firebase, which store authentication tokens in IndexedDB. |
| `🏷credentials`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | Also save the context's virtual WebAuthn credentials, as created by [Create Credential](#create-credential). This is not related to the `httpCredentials` argument of `New Context`, which is about HTTP authentication. |

**Return Type**: [`str`](#string-standard)


**Tags**:
- BrowserControl
- Getter

#### Documentation:
Saves the current active context storage state to a file.


Web apps use cookie-based or token-based authentication, where authenticated state is stored as [cookies](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Cookies) or in [local storage](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Storage). This keyword retrieves the storage state from authenticated contexts and saves it to disk. Then `New Context` can be created with prepopulated state.


Please note that the state file may contain secrets and should not be shared with people outside of your organisation.


Files in `${OUTPUTDIR}`/browser/state are automatically deleted when new test execution starts. To keep a state file over several executions, save it with `path` to a location outside of that folder. File path is returned by the keyword.


Example:


```text
Test Case
    `New context`
    `New Page`    https://login.page.html
    #  Perform login
    VAR    ${username: Secret}    %{USERNAME}    # Convert environment variable to secret
    VAR    ${password: Secret}    %{PASSWORD}    # Convert environment variable to secret
    `Fill Secret`    id=username    ${username}
    `Fill Secret`    id=password    ${password}
    `Click`    id=button
    `Get Text`    id=header    ==    Something
    #  Save storage to disk
    ${state_file} =    `Save Storage State`
    #  Create new context with saved state
    `New context`    storageState=${state_file}
    `New Page`    https://login.page.html
    #  Login is not needed because authentication is read from state file
    `Get Text`    id=header    ==    Something
```

[Comment >>](https://forum.robotframework.org/t//4318)


**In Electron applications:**


Fails with `Target.createTarget: Not supported` when an http or https origin that the application has visited is no longer open in a window: Playwright then opens a page of its own, which Electron does not allow. The local storage of `file://` pages is not saved.

| `vertical`| : [`str`](#string-standard) | = | `height` | Defines how far and in which direction to scroll vertically. It can be a positive or negative number. It can be the string `height` to scroll exactly one visible height down, or `-height` to scroll one visible height up. *Be aware that some pages do lazy loading and load more content once you scroll down.* The percentage of the current scrollable height is used and may change. Defaults to `height`. |
| `horizontal`| : [`str`](#string-standard) | = | `0` | Defines how far and in which direction to scroll horizontally. Works the same way as `vertical`, but positive values scroll to the right and negative values to the left. `width` scrolls exactly one visible range to the right. Defaults to `0`. |

### Select Options By

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Selector of the `\<select>` tag. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |
| `attribute`| : [`SelectAttribute`](#selectattribute-enum) |  |  | Attribute to select options by. Can be `value`, `label`, `text` or `index`. Where `label` and `text` are same. |
| `*values`|   |  |  | Values to select. |

**Return Type**: [`list`](#list-standard)`[`[`Any`](#any-standard)`]`


**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Selects options from select element found by `selector`.


Returns a list of the options which the keyword was able to select. The type of the list items matches the `attribute` definition. For example, if `attribute` equals `label`, the returned list contains label values. Or in case of `index`, it contains the selected indexes.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


If no values to select are passed, all options of the element are deselected. The keyword fails if none of the given values matches an option.


Example:


```text
${selected} =    `Select Options By`    select[name=preferred_channel]    label    Direct mail
List Should Contain Value    ${selected}    Direct mail
${selected} =    `Select Options By`    select[name=interests]    value    males    females    others
List Should Contain Value    ${selected}    males
List Should Contain Value    ${selected}    females
List Should Contain Value    ${selected}    others
Length Should Be    ${selected}    3
${selected} =    `Select Options By`    select[name=possible_channels]    index    0    2
List Should Contain Value    ${selected}    0
List Should Contain Value    ${selected}    2
${selected} =    `Select Options By`    select[name=interests]    text     Males    Females
List Should Contain Value    ${selected}    Males
List Should Contain Value    ${selected}    Females
```

The dictionary value is a list of formatters which are applied. Formatters for a defined keyword are always overwritten. An empty list will clear all formatters for the keyword. If `formatters` is an empty dictionary, then all formatters are cleared from all keywords, in the Global scope, regardless of the `scope` argument. |

Returns the formatters which were in use before this keyword was called. Formatters defined as lambda functions are not included in the returned value.


See type documentation of [FormatterKeywords](#formatterkeywords-enum) and [FormatingRules](#formatingrules-enum) for more information.


It is possible to define own formatters as lambda functions.


Example:


```text
`Set Assertion Formatters`    {"Get Text": ["strip", "normalize spaces"]}  # This will convert all kinds of spaces to a single space and remove spaces from the start and end of the string.
```

Presenter mode highlights elements found by keywords, which is useful for test debugging and demonstration. When enabled, the element is scrolled into view and highlighted with a border for a while to visually show what the keyword found.


The keyword returns the previous presenter mode value, allowing you to restore it later.


Example:


```text
${old_mode} =    Set Presenter Mode    True

...    style=dotted

```

### Set Selector Prefix

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `prefix`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) |  |  | Prefix for all selectors. Prefix and selector will be separated by a single space. Use `${None}` or `${EMPTY}` to disable the prefix. |
| `scope`| : [`Scope`](#scope-enum) | = | `Suite` | Scope defines the live time of that setting. Available values are `Global`, `Suite` or `Test` / `Task`. See [Scope Setting](#scope-setting) for more details. |

**Tags**:
- Config
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Sets the prefix for all selectors in the given scope.


Returns the previous value of the prefix.


Example:


```text
${old} =    `Set Selector Prefix`    iframe#embedded_page >>>
`Click`    button#login_btn       # Clicks on button inside iframe with the selector ``iframe#embedded_page >>> button#login_btn``
`Set Selector Prefix`    ${old}
```

Example will click on button with id `login_btn` inside iframe with id `embedded_page`. The resulting selector will be `iframe\#embedded_page >>> button\#login_btn`.


The effect of this prefix can be disabled by prefixing any selector with `!prefix `, with a trailing space, for single keyword calls, i.e. `!prefix id=btn_outside_a_frame`


[Get Element](#get-element), [Get Elements](#get-elements), [Get Element By](#get-element-by) and [Get Element By Role](#get-element-by-role) automatically prefix the returned selector with `!prefix ` so that it is possible to use them directly without setting the prefix to `${None}` before usage.

### Set Time

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `time`| : [`datetime`](#datetime-standard) |  |  | The time to set. Supports Robot Framework date and time format |
| `clock_type`| : [`ClockType`](#clocktype-enum) | = | `install` | The clock type to set. Default is `install`. |

**Tags**:
- Clock
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Sets the time of the browser's internal clock.


`fixed` makes `Date.now` and `new Date()` always return the same fake time, while all timers keep running.


`system` sets the current system time but does not trigger any timers.


`install` installs fake timers, which are used to manually control the flow of time in tests. They allow you to advance time, fire timers, and control the behavior of time-dependent functions.


How to use clock related keywords, see [Playwright clock documentation](https://playwright.dev/docs/clock). Also reviewing the Playwright [Clock API](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-clock) is recommended.

### Set Viewport Size

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `width`| : [`int`](#integer-standard) |  |  | Sets the width in pixels. |
| `height`| : [`int`](#integer-standard) |  |  | Sets the height in pixels. |

**Tags**:
- BrowserControl
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Sets the current page's viewport size to the specified dimensions.


In the case of multiple pages in a single browser, each page can have its own viewport size. However, `New Context` allows setting the viewport size (and more) for all later opened pages in the context at once.


[Set Viewport Size](#set-viewport-size) will resize the page. A lot of websites don't expect phones to change size, so you should set the viewport size with `New Context` before opening the page itself.


[Comment >>](https://forum.robotframework.org/t//4333)
