### Set Window Size

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `width`| : [`int`](#integer-standard) |  |  | The width of the content in pixels. |
| `height`| : [`int`](#integer-standard) |  |  | The height of the content in pixels. |
| `window`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | The window, see [Windows and pages](#windows-and-pages). Defaults to the window that shows the active page. |

**Return Type**: [`None`](#none-standard)


**Raises**:
- `AssertionError`: The window does not get the size within the library timeout, for example because the screen is smaller. The error names the size that the window has.


#### Documentation:
Gives a window the content size `width` x `height` and waits until it has it.


The content size is the area that the window's page shows, which its screenshots and its video have as well. A maximised, minimised or fullscreen window is made normal first. At a fractional display scale, the size can be off by up to 2 pixels, because the window's edges snap to whole device pixels.


Example:


```text
`Set Window Size`    1280    720
`Set Window Size`    1024    700    title=Settings
```

### Show Keyword Banner

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `show`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${True}` | If `True`, the banner is shown on the page. If `False`, the banner is not shown on the page. If `${None}`, the banner is shown on the page only when running in presenter mode. |
| `style`| : [`str`](#string-standard) | = | `${EMPTY}` | Additional CSS styles to be applied to the banner. These styles may override the existing ones for the banner. |
| `scope`| : [`Scope`](#scope-enum) | = | `Suite` | Scope defines the live time of that setting. Available values are `Global`, `Suite` or `Test` / `Task`. See [Scope Setting](#scope-setting) for more details. |

**Return Type**: [`dict`](#dictionary-standard)`[`[`str`](#string-standard)`, `[`bool`](#boolean-standard) | [`str`](#string-standard) | [`None`](#none-standard)`]`


**Tags**:
- Config
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Controls if the keyword banner is shown on page or not.


The keyword call banner is a CSS overlay that shows the currently executed keyword directly on the page. This is useful for debugging and for showing the test execution on video recordings. By default, the banner is not shown on the page except when running in presenter mode.


The banner can also be controlled by an import setting of the Browser library. (see [Importing](#importing) section)


Returns the previous settings as a dictionary with the keys `show` and `style`.


Example:


```text
Show Keyword Banner     True    top: 5px; bottom: auto; left: 5px; background-color: #00909077; font-size: 9px; color: black;   # Show banner on top left corner with custom styles
Show Keyword Banner     False   # Hide banner
```

### Start Coverage

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `🏷config_file`| : [`PathLike`](#path-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Optional path to [options file](https://www.npmjs.com/package/monocart-coverage-reports#options). If the file does not exist, it is ignored. |
| `🏷coverage_type`| : [`CoverageType`](#coveragetype-enum) | = | `all` | Type of coverage to start. Default is `all`. |
| `🏷path`| : [`Path`](#path-standard) | = | `.` | Absolute or relative directory path (relative to `${OUTPUT_DIR}/browser/coverage/`) where the coverage is stored in a directory with the page id name. |
| `🏷raw`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | Whether to save raw coverage data. Default is `False`. |
| `🏷reportAnonymousScripts`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | Whether to report anonymous scripts. Default is `False`. Only valid for JS coverage. |
| `🏷resetOnNavigation`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${True}` | Whether to reset coverage on navigation. Default is `True`. |

**Return Type**: [`str`](#string-standard)


**Tags**:
- Coverage
- Experimental
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Starts the coverage for the current page.


The `coverage_type` can be one of the following:


- `all`: Both [CSS](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-coverage/#coverage-start-css-coverage) and [JS](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-coverage/#coverage-start-js-coverage).
- `css`: [CSS](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-coverage/#coverage-start-css-coverage).
- `js`: [JS](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-coverage/#coverage-start-js-coverage).


Coverage must be started when the page is open and before any action is performed on the page. Coverage will be stored when calling the [Stop Coverage](#stop-coverage) keyword or when the page or context is closed. This is done automatically when using the auto closing.


The `raw` argument saves the raw coverage data in the coverage folder. The raw data is needed to combine multiple coverage reports into a single report. A single report can be created with the `rfbrowser coverage /path/to/basefolder/ /path/to/outputfolder/` command. Please note that the `raw` argument is ignored if the `config_file` is defined. In that case the user is responsible for also setting the raw reporter in the config file. To see more details about combining coverage data, run the `rfbrowser coverage --help` command.


Example:


```text
`New Page`
`Start Coverage`
`Go To`    ${LOGIN_URL}
Do Something In The Page
`Stop Coverage`
```

### Start Electron Application

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `executable_path`| : [`Path`](#path-standard) |  |  | The Electron executable, as a path or as a command found on `PATH`. A relative path is relative to the working directory of the test run. For an app that is run by the plain Electron binary, pass the app folder in `args`. |
| `args`| : [`list`](#list-standard)`[`[`str`](#string-standard)`]` \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Command-line arguments for the application. |
| `env`| : [`dict`](#dictionary-standard)`[`[`str`](#string-standard)`, `[`str`](#string-standard)`]` \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Environment variables of the application. If not given, the application gets the environment of the test run without `ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE`, which runs started from VS Code have and which would make Electron run as plain Node.js. |
| `cwd`| : [`Path`](#path-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Working directory of the application. A relative path is relative to the working directory of the test run, which is also the default. |
| `timeout`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | How long to wait for the application to start and open its first window. Defaults to the library timeout. |
| `record_video`| : [`RecordVideo`](#recordvideo-typeddict) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Records a video of the application's windows, see [RecordVideo](#recordvideo-typeddict) for the folder, size, frame rate and the annotations of the performed actions. An empty dictionary records with the defaults: Browser's video folder `browser/video` in the output directory and a size of 1280x720. A larger window is scaled down to fit, a smaller one is shown at its own size with a grey margin. The log embeds the video, and the file is complete once the application has closed. Recording needs Playwright's ffmpeg, which comes with any browser that Browser installs, but not with `rfbrowser init --skip-browsers`. |
| `record_har`| : [`RecordHar`](#recordhar-typeddict) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Records the network traffic of the application's windows into a [HAR](http://www.softwareishard.com/blog/har-12-spec/) file, as `recordHar` of the Browser library's `New Context`: a dictionary with the `path` of the file and optionally `omitContent`. A relative path is relative to the output directory. The file is written when the application closes. |
| `tracing`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) \| [`Path`](#path-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Records a Playwright trace of the application, as `tracing` of the Browser library's `New Context`: `True` saves it in `browser/traces` in the output directory, named after the application's context, and a `*.zip` path or a folder saves it there. Give a path to know the file's name. The variable or environment variable `ROBOT_FRAMEWORK_BROWSER_TRACING` set to `True` traces every application. The trace is saved when the application closes and shows the keyword calls as groups. Open it with `rfbrowser show-trace /path/to/trace.zip`. |
| `color_scheme`| : [`ColorScheme`](#colorscheme-enum) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | The color scheme that the windows report for `prefers-color-scheme`: `light` or `dark`. By default, and with `null`, the application decides, as it does outside of tests. Set it for tests that compare screenshots, so that they look the same on every machine. |
| `locale`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | The locale of the windows, for example `de-DE`. It sets the language that the pages report and their number and date formats. Defaults to the system's. The main process keeps the system's locale; `--lang` in `args` sets it there. |
| `timezone_id`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | The time zone of the windows, for example `Europe/Berlin`. Defaults to the system's. The main process keeps the system's time zone; `TZ` in `env` sets it there. |
| `bypass_csp`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | Bypasses the Content Security Policy of the windows, including Trusted Types, as `bypassCSP` of the Browser library's `New Context`. Features that add scripts to a page need it in applications with a strict policy, for example [Record Selector](#record-selector) in VS Code. An application can load its first window before the option takes effect, so the keyword loads the windows that are open once more. It also applies to webviews and frames, so that policy problems of the application go unnoticed. Switch it on only where a feature needs it. |

**Return Type**: [`tuple`](#tuple-standard)`[`[`str`](#string-standard)`, `[`NewPageDetails`](#newpagedetails-typeddict)`]` — A tuple of the application id and the page details of the first window. The page details contain the page id and the path of the video, or an empty string if no video is recorded.


**Raises**:
- `ValueError`: The executable is not found.


#### Documentation:
Starts an Electron application and makes its first window the active page.


The application becomes the active application. Its windows are pages, so Browser keywords like [Click](#click) and [Get Text](#get-text) work on them, and windows the application opens later can be selected with [Switch Window](#switch-window). [Close Electron Application](#close-electron-application) and automatic closing end the application.


Example:


```text
${app}    ${page} =    `Start Electron Application`    /opt/my-app/my-app
`Get Title`    ==    My App
`Start Electron Application`    ${ELECTRON}    args=${{ [$EXECDIR + "/app"] }}
`Start Electron Application`    /opt/my-app/my-app    tracing=True    record_har={'path': 'my-app.har'}
`Start Electron Application`    /opt/my-app/my-app    color_scheme=dark    locale=de-DE
`Start Electron Application`    /opt/my-app/my-app    record_video={'showActions': {'position': 'bottom'}}
```

### Stop Coverage


**Return Type**: [`Path`](#path-standard) | [`None`](#none-standard)


**Tags**:
- Coverage
- Getter

#### Documentation:
Stops the coverage for the current page.


Creates a coverage report by using [monocart-coverage-reports](https://www.npmjs.com/package/monocart-coverage-reports) To see the default and all possible options, see [options.js](https://github.com/cenfun/monocart-coverage-reports/blob/HEAD/lib/default/options.js) file for more details.


If coverage was not started, the keyword returns `None`. Otherwise it returns the path to the generated HTML report file, or the path to the coverage folder if no HTML file is found from the folder. The latter can happen when the report format or output folder has been changed with the `config_file` argument of the [Start Coverage](#start-coverage) keyword.

### Switch Electron Application

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `application`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | The application id that [Start Electron Application](#start-electron-application) returned. |

**Return Type**: [`str`](#string-standard) — The id of the application that was active before.


#### Documentation:
Makes another open application the active one.


Browser keywords then act on the active page of that application.


Example:


```text
${first}    ${_} =    `Start Electron Application`    /opt/my-app/my-app
`Start Electron Application`    /opt/other-app/other-app
`Switch Electron Application`    ${first}
```

### Switch Page

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `id`| : [`NewPageDetails`](#newpagedetails-typeddict) \| [`SelectionType`](#selectiontype-enum) \| [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | The id or alias of the page to switch to. Example: `page=8baf2991-5eaf-444d-a318-8045f914e96a` or `NEW`. Can be a string or a dictionary returned by `New Page` Keyword. A page id can be fetched from the browser catalog when returned by `Get Browser Catalog`. `NEW` can be used to switch to a pop-up that just has been opened by the webpage, `CURRENT` can be used to switch to the active page of a different context or browser, identified by their id. |
| `context`| : [`SelectionType`](#selectiontype-enum) \| [`str`](#string-standard) | = | `CURRENT` | The context in which to search for that page. `CURRENT` for the currently active context, `ALL` to search in all open contexts or the id of the context where to switch page. |
| `browser`| : [`SelectionType`](#selectiontype-enum) \| [`str`](#string-standard) | = | `CURRENT` | The browser in which to search for that page. `CURRENT` for the currently active browser, `ALL` to search in all open browsers or the id of the browser where to switch page. |

**Return Type**: [`str`](#string-standard)


**Tags**:
- BrowserControl
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Switches the active browser page to another open page by `id` or `NEW`.


Returns a stable identifier `id` for the previous page. See [Browser, Context and Page](#browser-context-and-page) for more information about Page and related concepts.


If a page id is given, the `context` and `browser` arguments are ignored and the page is searched from all open browsers.


`NEW` may time out if no new page is opened before the library timeout expires.


Example:


```text
`Click`           button#pops_up    # Open new page
${previous} =    `Switch Page`      NEW
```

[Comment >>](https://forum.robotframework.org/t//4336)


**In Electron applications:**


Each window of an application is a page, and so are the `\<webview>` and `WebContentsView` elements it shows. `NEW` takes the newest page if it is newer than the active page, which can be a `\<webview>` that loaded after a new window. [Switch Window](#switch-window) switches to a window by its title instead. Select a `\<webview>` or `WebContentsView` by its page id, which [Get Electron Application Catalog](#get-electron-application-catalog) returns with its title. `browser` takes an application id.

---

### Switch Window

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `window`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | The window, as `title=\<title>`, as a regular expression `title=/\<pattern>/\<flags>` or as an id from [Get Window Ids](#get-window-ids), see [Windows and pages](#windows-and-pages), or the page id of its page, as [Switch Page](#switch-page) takes it, or `NEW` for the newest page. A title suits a window that the application opens best, because the keyword waits until the window shows it. `NEW` takes the newest page if it is newer than the active page, as [Switch Page](#switch-page) does: that can be a `\<webview>` that loaded after the window, or after a switch back to an older window, a page that was open before. |

**Return Type**: [`str`](#string-standard) — The id of the page that was active before. [Switch Window](#switch-window) and [Switch Page](#switch-page) switch back to it.


**Raises**:
- `AssertionError`: No window matches, or the page is not a window's own page. The active page then stays the same. For a title, an expression or a window id, the keyword finds the window's page in Browser's catalog by the page's title, so the page needs a title that no other page of the application has. Otherwise, switch with the page id.


#### Documentation:
Makes the own page of a window the active page and returns the id of the page that was active before.


Browser keywords then act on that page, and the window comes to the front. [Switch Page](#switch-page) does the same for any page; [Switch Window](#switch-window) switches only to windows and fails instead of switching to a `\<webview>` or `WebContentsView`.


Example:


```text
`Click`    text=Settings
${previous} =    `Switch Window`    title=Settings
`Click`    text=Save
`Switch Window`    ${previous}
```

### Take Screenshot

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `filename`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `robotframework-browser-screenshot-{index}` | Filename into which to save. The file will be saved into the Robot Framework `${OUTPUTDIR}`/browser/screenshot directory by default, but it can be overwritten by providing a custom path or filename. String `{index}` in the filename will be replaced with a rolling number. Use this to not overwrite filenames. If filename equals to UUID (case insensitive), then the filename is created by Python uuid; [https://docs.python.org/3/library/uuid.html](https://docs.python.org/3/library/uuid.html). If filename equals to EMBED (case insensitive) or `${NONE}`, then the screenshot is embedded as a Base64 image into the log.html. The image is saved temporarily to the disk and a warning is displayed if removing the temporary file fails. The `${OUTPUTDIR}`/browser/screenshot directory is removed at the first suite startup. |
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Take a screenshot of the element matched by selector. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. If not provided, take a screenshot of the current viewport. |
| `🏷crop`| : [`BoundingBox`](#boundingbox-typeddict) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Crops the taken screenshot to the given box. It takes the same dictionary as returned from [Get BoundingBox](#get-boundingbox). Cropping only works on a page screenshot, so when no selector is given. |
| `🏷disableAnimations`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | When set to `True`, stops CSS animations, CSS transitions and Web Animations. Animations get different treatment depending on their duration:  - finite animations are fast-forwarded to completion, so they'll fire the transitionend event.  - infinite animations are cancelled to initial state, and then played over after the screenshot. |
| `🏷fileType`| : [`ScreenshotFileTypes`](#screenshotfiletypes-enum) | = | `png` | `png` or `jpeg`. Specifies the screenshot type, defaults to `png`. |
| `🏷fullPage`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | When `True`, takes a screenshot of the full scrollable page, instead of the currently visible viewport. Defaults to `False`. |
| `🏷highlight_selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Highlights elements while taking the screenshot. Highlight method is `playwright`. This highlighting also automatically happens if the Robot Framework variable `${ROBOT_FRAMEWORK_BROWSER_FAILING_SELECTOR}` is set to a selector string and is available on page. This is the case if `highlight_on_failure` has been set to `True` when importing Browser library. |
| `🏷log_screenshot`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${True}` | When set to `False` the screenshot is taken but not logged into log.html. |
| `🏷mask`| : [`list`](#list-standard)`[`[`str`](#string-standard)`]` \| [`str`](#string-standard) | = | `${EMPTY}` | Specify selectors that should be masked when the screenshot is taken. Masked elements will be overlaid with a pink box `\#FF00FF` that completely covers their bounding box. The argument can take a single selector string or a list of selector strings if multiple different elements should be masked. |
| `🏷maskColor`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Specify the color of the overlay box for masked elements, in CSS color format. Default color is pink \#FF00FF. |
| `🏷omitBackground`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | Hides the default white background and allows capturing screenshots with transparency. Not applicable to jpeg images. |
| `🏷quality`| : [`int`](#integer-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | The quality of the image, between 0-100. Not applicable to png images. |
| `🏷scale`| : [`Scale`](#scale-enum) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | `css` or `device`. `css` will reduce the image size and `device` keeps the image in its original size. Defaults to `device`. |
| `🏷return_as`| : [`ScreenshotReturnType`](#screenshotreturntype-enum) | = | `path_string` | Defines what this keyword returns. Possible values are documented in [ScreenshotReturnType](#screenshotreturntype-enum). It can be either a path to the screenshot file as string or Path object, or the image data as bytes or base64 encoded string. When the screenshot is embedded into the log, `path_string` returns the string `EMBED`. |
| `🏷timeout`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Maximum time how long taking the screenshot can last, defaults to the library timeout. Supports Robot Framework time format, like 10s or 1 min, pass 0 to disable the timeout. The default value can be changed by using the [Set Browser Timeout](#set-browser-timeout) keyword. |

**Return Type**: [`str`](#string-standard) | [`bytes`](#bytes-standard) | [`Path`](#path-standard) | [`None`](#none-standard)


**Tags**:
- PageContent

#### Documentation:
Takes a screenshot of the current window or element and saves it to disk.


Keyword uses strict mode if selector is defined. See [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


Example


```text
`Take Screenshot`                                 # Takes screenshot from page with default filename
`Take Screenshot`   selector=id=username_field    # Captures element in image
# Takes screenshot with jpeg extension, defines image quality and timeout how long taking screenshot should last
`Take Screenshot`   fullPage=True    fileType=jpeg    quality=50    timeout=10s
`Take Screenshot`   EMBED                         # Screenshot is embedded as Base64 image to the log.html.
`Take Screenshot`   UUID                          # Takes screenshot from page with filename generated by: https://docs.python.org/3/library/uuid.html.
```

### Type Secret

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Selector of the text field. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |
| `secret`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`Secret`](#secret-standard) |  |  | Supports Robot Framework 7.4 Secret type as normal variable (with curly braces). Also environment variable name with % prefix or a local variable with $ prefix that has the secret text value (without curly braces). |
| `delay`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) | = | `0:00:00` | Delay between the single key strokes. It may be either a number or a Robot Framework time string. Time strings are fully explained in an appendix of Robot Framework User Guide. Defaults to `0 ms`. Example: `50 ms` |
| `clear`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${True}` | Set to `False` if the field should not be cleared before typing. Defaults to `True`. |

**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Types the given `secret` into the text field found by `selector`.


This keyword does not log the secret in Robot Framework logs, but if Playwright debug logs are enabled, the secret will be visible as plain text in the Playwright debug logs, regardless of the Robot Framework log level or how `secret` is resolved.


This keyword supports Robot Framework 7.4 [Secret](https://robotframework.org/robotframework/latest/RobotFrameworkUserGuide.html#secret-variables) variable type, which is the recommended way if you are using Robot Framework 7.4 or newer.


For older Robot Framework versions the keyword supports resolving secrets from environment variables and Robot Framework variables in the following ways. The keyword resolves the `secret` from a Robot Framework variable internally, when the `secret` variable is prefixed with `$`, without the curly braces. Example: `$Password` will resolve to the `${Password}` Robot Framework variable.


If the `secret` variable is prefixed with `%`, the library will resolve the corresponding environment variable. Example: `%ENV_PWD` will resolve to the `%{ENV_PWD}` environment variable.


**Using normal Robot Framework variables like `${password}`, which are not Secret type variables, will not work!**


**Normal plain text will not work.** If you want to use plain text, use the [Type Text](#type-text) keyword instead.


This keyword also works with a cryptographic cipher text that has been encrypted by CryptoLibrary. See [CryptoLibrary](https://github.com/Snooz82/robotframework-crypto) for more details.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


See [Type Text](#type-text) for details.


Example


```text
`Type Secret`    input#username_field    ${username}    # Keyword resolves ${username} variable value from Robot Framework Secret type variable
`Type Secret`    input#username_field    $username      # Keyword resolves ${username} variable value from Robot Framework variables
`Type Secret`    input#username_field    %username      # Keyword resolves $USERNAME/%USERNAME% variable value from environment variables
```

[Comment >>](https://forum.robotframework.org/t//4338)

### Type Text

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Selector of the text field. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |
| `txt`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Text for the text field. |
| `delay`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) | = | `0:00:00` | Delay between the single key strokes. It may be either a number or a Robot Framework time string. Time strings are fully explained in an appendix of Robot Framework User Guide. Defaults to `0 ms`. Example: `50 ms` |
| `clear`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${True}` | Set to `False` if the field should not be cleared before typing. Defaults to `True`. |

**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Types the given `txt` into the text field found by `selector`.


Sends a `keydown`, `keypress/input`, and `keyup` event for each character in the text.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


See [Fill Text](#fill-text) for filling the full text at once.


Example


```text
`Type Text`    input#username_field    user
`Type Text`    input#username_field    user    delay=10 ms    clear=No
```

### Uncheck Checkbox

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Selector of the checkbox. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |
| `force`| : [`bool`](#boolean-standard) | = | `${False}` | Set to `True` to skip Playwright's [Actionability checks](https://playwright.dev/docs/actionability). |

**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Unchecks the checkbox found by `selector`.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


Does nothing if the element is not checked/selected.

### Upload File By Selector

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Identifies the file input element. |
| `path`| : [`PathLike`](#path-standard) \| [`FileUploadBuffer`](#fileuploadbuffer-typeddict) |  |  | Path to the file or folder to be uploaded. Can also be a [FileUploadBuffer](#fileuploadbuffer-typeddict) dictionary. |
| `*extra_paths`| : [`PathLike`](#path-standard) |  |  | Additional paths to files or folders to be uploaded. |

**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Setter

#### Documentation:
Uploads file from `path` to file input element matched by selector.


Fails if the upload is not done before the library timeout. Therefore it may be necessary to increase the timeout with [Set Browser Timeout](#set-browser-timeout). It is possible to upload multiple files or folders by defining additional files or folders in `extra_paths`.


If a path is a directory, all files from the directory are uploaded. Subdirectories are not included. It is possible to upload files and directories with the same keyword. The keyword fails if a given path does not exist.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


If `path` is a [FileUploadBuffer](#fileuploadbuffer-typeddict) dictionary, then the structure should be:


```text
{
  'name': ``str``,
  'mimeType': ``str``,
  'buffer': ``str``
}
```

If `path` argument is [FileUploadBuffer](#fileuploadbuffer-typeddict), then `extra_paths` argument is not supported and using it will raise an error.


Upload single file example:


```text
`Upload File By Selector`    //input[@type='file']    big_file.zip
```

Upload many files example:


```text
`Upload File By Selector`    //input[@type='file']    file1.zip    file2.zip    file3.zip
```

Upload folder example:


```text
`Upload File By Selector`    //input[@type='file']    /path/to/folder
```

Upload as buffer example:


```text
${text} =    Get File    /path/to/file    # Read file from disk
VAR    &{buffer}    name=not_here.txt    mimeType=text/plain    buffer=${text}    # Create buffer dictionary
`Upload File By Selector`    id=file_chooser    ${buffer}    # Upload buffer
```

### Wait For

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `*promises`| : `Future` |  |  | Promises to wait for. |

**Tags**:
- Wait

#### Documentation:
Waits for promises to finish and returns results from them.


Returns a single result if only one promise is waited for. Otherwise it returns a list of results in the same order as the promises were given. If one of the promises fails, then this keyword will fail.


See [Promise To](#promise-to) for more information about promises.


For general waiting of elements please see [Implicit waiting](#implicit-waiting).


Example:


```text
${promise}=    `Promise To`            `Wait For Response`     matcher=     timeout=3
`Click`         \#delayed_request
${body}=       `Wait For`              ${promise}
```

### Wait For Alert

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `action`| : [`DialogAction`](#dialogaction-enum) |  |  | How to handle the alert. Can be `accept` or `dismiss`. |
| `prompt_input`| : [`str`](#string-standard) | = | `${EMPTY}` | The value to enter into the prompt. Only valid if the `action` argument equals `accept`. Defaults to an empty string. |
| `text`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Optional text to verify the dialog text with. |
| `timeout`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Optional timeout in Robot Framework time format. Defaults to the library timeout. |

**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Wait

#### Documentation:
Returns a promise to wait for next dialog on page, handles it with `action` and optionally verifies the dialogs text.


Dialog/alert can be any of alert, beforeunload, confirm or prompt.


The main difference between this keyword and [Handle Future Dialogs](#handle-future-dialogs) is that the [Handle Future Dialogs](#handle-future-dialogs) keyword is automatically set as a promise, but this keyword must be called as an argument to the [Promise To](#promise-to) keyword. Also this keyword can optionally verify the dialog text and returns it. If the `text` argument is `None` or is not set, the dialog text is not verified.


Example with returning text:


```text
${promise} =         `Promise To`    `Wait For Alert`    action=accept
`Click`               id=alerts
${text} =            `Wait For`      ${promise}
Should Be Equal      ${text}         Am an alert
```

Example with text verification:


```text
${promise} =       `Promise To`    Wait For Alert    action=accept    text=Am an alert
Click              id=alerts
${text} =          `Wait For`      ${promise}
```

[Comment >>](https://forum.robotframework.org/t//4343)

### Wait For Alerts

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `actions`| : [`list`](#list-standard)`[`[`DialogAction`](#dialogaction-enum)`]` |  |  | List of how to handle the alerts. Can be `accept` or `dismiss`. |
| `prompt_inputs`| : [`list`](#list-standard)`[`[`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard)`]` |  |  | List of the values to enter into the prompts. Only valid if the corresponding action equals `accept`. Use `None` if no input is needed. |
| `texts`| : [`list`](#list-standard)`[`[`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard)`]` |  |  | List of optional texts to verify the dialog texts with. Use `None` if text verification should be disabled. |
| `timeout`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Optional timeout in Robot Framework time format. Defaults to the library timeout. The timeout is applied to each alert separately. |

**Return Type**: [`list`](#list-standard)`[`[`str`](#string-standard)`]`


**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Wait

#### Documentation:
Returns a promise to wait for multiple dialogs on a page.


Handles each alert/dialog with `actions` and optionally verifies the dialog texts. Dialog/alert can be any of alert, beforeunload, confirm or prompt.


There must be an equal amount of items in the `actions`, `prompt_inputs` and `texts` lists. Use `None` if texts and/or prompt inputs are not needed.


This keyword works in the same way as [Wait For Alert](#wait-for-alert), but it can handle multiple alerts with one promise. Like the [Wait For Alert](#wait-for-alert) keyword, this keyword must be called as an argument to the [Promise To](#promise-to) keyword.


Example to handle two alerts, first one is accepted and second one is dismissed:


```text
${promise} =    Promise To
...    Wait For Alerts
...    ["accept", "dismiss"]
...    [None, None]
...    [None, None]
Click    id=alerts
${texts} =    Wait For    ${promise}
```

Example to handle confirm and prompt alert. Example assumes that the first is a confirm and second one is prompt:


```text
${promise} =    Promise To
...    Wait For Alerts
...    ["dismiss", "accept"]
...    [None, "I am a prompt"]
...    ["First alert accepted?", None]
Click    id=confirmAndPrompt
${texts} =    Wait For    ${promise}
```

### Wait For Condition

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `condition`| : [`ConditionInputs`](#conditioninputs-enum) |  |  | A condition, defined with Browser getter keywords, without the word `Get`. |
| `*args`| : [`Any`](#any-standard) |  |  | Arguments to pass to the condition keyword. |
| `🏷timeout`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Timeout to wait for the condition to become True. Uses default timeout of the library if not set. As the other assertion keywords this timeout only influences the time the assertion is retried. The browser timeout is used to wait for the element to be found. |
| `🏷message`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Overrides the default error message. |

**Return Type**: [`Any`](#any-standard)


**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Wait

#### Documentation:
Waits for a condition, defined with Browser getter keywords, to become True.


This keyword is basically just a wrapper around our assertion keywords, but with a timeout. It can be used to wait for anything that also can be asserted with our keywords.


In comparison to Robot Framework's `Wait Until Keyword Succeeds` this keyword is more readable and easier to use, but is limited to Browser library's assertion keywords.


The easiest way to use this keyword is first starting with an assertion keyword with assertion like: [Get Text](#get-text)


Start:


```text
`Get Text`    id=status_bar   contains    Done
```

Then you replace the word `Get` with [Wait For Condition](#wait-for-condition) and if necessary add the timeout argument.


End:


```text
`Wait For Condition`    Text    id=status_bar   contains    Done
```

Example usage:


```text
`Wait For Condition`    Element States    id=cdk-overlay-0    ==    detached
`Wait For Condition`    Element States     //h1    contains    visible    editable    enabled    timeout=2 s
`Wait For Condition`    Title    should start with    Robot
`Wait For Condition`    Url    should end with    robotframework.org
```

### Wait For Elements State

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | Selector of the corresponding object. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |
| `state`| : [`ElementState`](#elementstate-enum) | = | `${<ElementState.visible: 4>}` | See [ElementState](#elementstate-enum) for explanation. |
| `timeout`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | uses default timeout from library if not set. |
| `message`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | overrides the default error message. The `message` argument accepts `{selector}`, `{function}`, and `{timeout}` [format](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str.format) options. The `{function}` formatter is the `state` argument value for the states which are waited for by Playwright, that are `attached`, `detached`, `visible`, `hidden`, `stable`, `enabled`, `disabled` and `editable`. For all other states, it is the JavaScript expression which is evaluated for the element. |

**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Wait

#### Documentation:
Waits for the element found by `selector` to satisfy state option.


Note that Browser library has [Implicit waiting](#implicit-waiting) mechanisms. Depending on the situation you might not need to use [Wait for Elements State](#wait-for-elements-state).


If users experience reliability issues with this keyword, consider using [Wait for Condition](#wait-for-condition) with [Get Element States](#get-element-states) keyword instead. [Wait For Elements State](#wait-for-elements-state) uses features of Playwright to wait for element states. However, in some situations these features might not work as expected. [Wait for Condition](#wait-for-condition) with [Get Element States](#get-element-states) is more robust as it uses Browser library's own waiting mechanisms that actively poll the state of an element.


State options are appearing in or disappearing from the DOM, becoming visible or hidden, and the other states listed in [ElementState](#elementstate-enum). If at the moment of calling the keyword, the selector already satisfies the condition, the keyword will return immediately.


If the selector doesn't satisfy the condition within the timeout the keyword will FAIL.


The states `focused` and `defocused` are not supported with iframe selectors, which contain `>>>`. In that case the keyword raises an error and suggests to use [Wait For Condition](#wait-for-condition) with [Get Element States](#get-element-states) instead.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


Example:


```text
`Wait For Elements State`    //h1    visible    timeout=2 s
`Wait For Elements State`    //h1    focused    1s
```

### Wait For Function

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `function`| : [`str`](#string-standard) |  |  | A valid javascript function or a javascript function body. For example `() => true` and `true` will behave similarly. |
| `selector`| : [`str`](#string-standard) | = | `${EMPTY}` | Selector to resolve and pass to the JavaScript function. This will be the first argument the function receives. If a selector is given, `function` must be a function with an argument which receives the element handle. For example `(element) => document.activeElement === element`. See the [Finding elements](#finding-elements) section for details about the selectors. |
| `polling`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) | = | `raf` | Default polling value of `raf` polls in a callback for `requestAnimationFrame`. Any other value for polling will be parsed as a Robot Framework time for the interval between polls. |
| `timeout`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Uses default timeout of the library if not set. |
| `message`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | overrides the default error message. The `message` argument accepts `{selector}`, `{function}`, and `{timeout}` [format](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#str.format) options. |

**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Wait

#### Documentation:
Polls JavaScript expression or function in browser until it returns a (JavaScript) truthy value.


Keyword uses strict mode, see [Finding elements](#finding-elements) for more details about strict mode.


Example usage:


```text
${promise}      `Promise To`      `Wait For Function`    element => element.style.width=="100%"    selector=\#progress_bar    timeout=4s
`Click`         \#progress_bar
`Wait For`      ${promise}
```

### Wait For Load State

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `state`| : [`PageLoadStates`](#pageloadstates-enum) | = | `load` | State to wait for, defaults to `load`. Possible values are `load`, `domcontentloaded`, `networkidle` and `commit`. |
| `timeout`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Timeout supports Robot Framework time format. Uses browser timeout if not set. |

**Tags**:
- PageContent
- Wait

#### Documentation:
Waits until the page reaches the required load state.


This resolves when the page reaches a required load state, load by default. The navigation must have been committed when this method is called. If current document has already reached the required state, resolves immediately.


If the state has been already reached while loading current document, the underlying Playwright will resolve immediately. Can be one of:


```text
``load`` - wait for the load event to be fired.
``domcontentloaded`` - wait for the DOMContentLoaded event to be fired.
``networkidle`` - DISCOURAGED wait until there are no network connections for at least 500 ms.
``commit`` - not supported by this keyword, the keyword returns immediately without waiting.
```

If the wait times out, the page's load report is logged: whether its navigation committed, how far the document got and which requests were still open.


Example:


```text
`Go To`                         ${URL}
`Wait For Load State`    domcontentloaded    timeout=3s
```

### Wait For Navigation

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `url`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`RegExp`](#regexp-custom) |  |  | Expected navigation target address, either a Glob-Pattern (a plain string without wildcards matches exactly) or a JavaScript-like regex wrapped in `/` symbols. |
| `timeout`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Timeout supports Robot Framework time format. Uses default timeout if not set. |
| `wait_until`| : [`PageLoadStates`](#pageloadstates-enum) | = | `load` | When to consider the operation succeeded, defaults to load. Events can be either: `domcontentloaded` - consider operation to be finished when the DOMContentLoaded event is fired. `load` - consider operation to be finished when the load event is fired. `networkidle` - consider operation to be finished when there are no network connections for at least 500 ms. `commit` - consider operation to be finished when network response is received and the document started loading. |

**Tags**:
- HTTP
- Wait

#### Documentation:
Waits until the page has navigated to the given `url`.


The keyword works only when the page is loaded and it does not work if only the URL fragment changes. Example: if [https://marketsquare.github.io/robotframework-browser/Browser.html](https://marketsquare.github.io/robotframework-browser/Browser.html) changes to [https://marketsquare.github.io/robotframework-browser/Browser.html\#Wait%20For%20Navigation](https://marketsquare.github.io/robotframework-browser/Browser.html#Wait%20For%20Navigation) the keyword will fail.


Example:


```text
`Go To`                  ${ROOT_URL}/redirector.html
`Wait for navigation`    ${ROOT_URL}/posted.html    wait_until=${wait_until}
```

If the wait times out, the page's load report is logged: whether its navigation committed, how far the document got and which requests were still open.

### Wait For Request

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `matcher`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`RegExp`](#regexp-custom) | = | `${EMPTY}` | Request URL matcher. Can be a string (Glob-Pattern), a JavaScript RegExp (enclosed in `/` with optional trailing flags) or a JavaScript arrow-function that receives the [Request](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-request) object and returns a boolean. By default (with an empty string) the first request is matched. For additional information, see the Playwright [waitForRequest](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-wait-for-request) documentation. |
| `timeout`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Timeout supports Robot Framework time format. Uses default timeout if not set. |

**Return Type**: [`DotDict`](#mapping-standard) | [`Any`](#any-standard)


**Tags**:
- HTTP
- Wait

#### Documentation:
Waits for a request matching `matcher` to be made.


Only the request is awaited, not its response. See [Wait For Response](#wait-for-response) if the response is needed.


The returned object is a dictionary with the keys `url`, `method`, `headers` and `postData`. `headers` is a dictionary of request headers. `postData` is `None` if the request has no body, a dictionary if the body is valid JSON and otherwise the body as a string.


See [Wait For Response](#wait-for-response) for more details about the matcher.


**CAUTION:** Before Browser library 17.0.0, the `matcher` argument was always either a regex or JS function. But the regex did not need to be in slashes. The most simple way to migrate to the new syntax is to add slashes around the matcher. So `/api/get/json` becomes `//api/get/json/`.


[Comment >>](https://forum.robotframework.org/t//4348)

### Wait For Response

#### Arguments:

| | | | | |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `matcher`| : [`str`](#string-standard) \| [`RegExp`](#regexp-custom) | = | `${EMPTY}` | Response URL matcher. Can be a string (Glob-Pattern), a JavaScript RegExp (enclosed in `/` with optional trailing flags) or a JavaScript arrow-function that receives the Response object and returns a boolean. By default (with an empty string) the first response is matched. For additional information, see the Playwright [page.waitForResponse](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-wait-for-response) documentation. |
| `timeout`| : [`timedelta`](#timedelta-standard) \| [`None`](#none-standard) | = | `${None}` | Timeout supports Robot Framework time format. Uses default timeout if not set. |

**Return Type**: [`DotDict`](#mapping-standard) | [`Any`](#any-standard)


**Tags**:
- HTTP
- Wait

#### Documentation:
Waits for a response matching `matcher` and returns the response as a Robot Framework dictionary.


The keyword waits until the response headers are received and then reads the response body.


The response, which is returned by this keyword, is a Robot Framework dictionary with the following attributes:


- `status` \<int> The status code of the response.
- `statusText` \<str> Status text corresponding to `status`, e.g. OK or INTERNAL SERVER ERROR. This may not be available for all browsers.
- `body` \<dict | str> The response body. If the body can be parsed as a JSON object, it will be returned as Python dictionary, otherwise it is returned as a string. It is `None` if the body could not be read and the key is missing altogether if the response body is empty.
- `headers` \<dict> A dictionary containing all response headers.
- `ok` \<bool> Whether the request was successful, i.e. the `status` is in the range 200-299.
- `request` \<dict> containing `method` \<str>, `headers` \<dict> and `postData` \<dict> | \<str>
- `url` \<str> url of the response.


**CAUTION:** Before Browser library 17.0.0, the `matcher` argument was always either a regex or JS function. But the regex did not need to be in slashes. The most simple way to migrate to the new syntax is to add slashes around the matcher. So `/api/get/json` becomes `//api/get/json/`.


###### Matcher Examples:

###### Glob-Pattern:

Glob-Patterns are strings that can contain wildcards. Possible wildcards/patterns are:


- `*` matches any number of characters, except `/`
- `**` matches any number of characters, including `/`
- `?` matches one character, except `/`
- `[abc]` matches one character in the brackets (in this example `a`, `b` or `c`)
- `[a-z]` matches one character in the range (in this example `a` to `z`)
- `{foo,bar,baz}` matches one of the strings in the braces (in this example `foo`, `bar` or `baz`)


Example:


```text
`Wait For Response`    **/api/get/text    # matches any response with url ending with /api/get/text. example: https://browser.fi/api/get/text
```

###### RegExp:

Regular Expressions are JavaScript regular expressions enclosed in `/` with optional trailing flags. Be aware that backslashes need to be escaped in Robot Framework, e.g. `\\w` instead of `\w`. See [regex101](https://regex101.com) for more information on Regular Expressions.


Example:


```text
`Wait For Response`    /http://\\w+:\\d+/api/get/text/i    # matches any response with url ending with /api/get/text and containing http:// followed by any word and port. example: http://localhost:8080/api/get/text
```

###### JavaScript Arrow-Function:

JavaScript Arrow-Functions are anonymous JavaScript functions that receive the [Response](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-response) object and return a boolean.


Example:


```text
`Wait For Response`    response => response.url() === 'http://localhost/api/post' && response.status() === 200    # matches any response with url http://localhost/api/post and status code 200
```

###### Robot Examples:

Synchronous Example:


```text
`Click`                \#delayed_request    # Creates response which should be waited before next actions
`Wait For Response`    matcher=/http://\\w+:\\d+/api/get/text/i
`Click`                \#save
```

Asynchronous Example:


```text
${promise} =    `Promise To`    `Wait For Response`    timeout=60s
`Click`           \#delayed_request    # Creates response which should be waited before pressing save.
`Click`           \#next
`Wait For`        ${promise}            # Waits for the response
`Click`           \#save
```

JavaScript Function Example:


```text
`Click`               \#delayed_request    # Creates response which should be waited before pressing save.
`Wait For Response`   response => response.url().endsWith('json') && response.request().method() === 'GET'
```

## Data types

### Any (Standard)

#### Documentation:



Any value is accepted. No conversion is done.


#### Converted Types:

- Any

---

### AreaFields (Enum)

#### Documentation:



Enumeration that defines which coordinates of an area should be selected.


`ALL` defines that all fields are selected and a dictionary with all information is returned.


#### Allowed Values:

- `top`
- `left`
- `bottom`
- `right`
- `ALL`

#### Converted Types:

- string

---

### AriaSnapshotMode (Enum)

#### Documentation:



Defines the mode of the AriaSnapshot.


| Value | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `default` | Standard aria snapshot. |
| `ai` | Snapshot optimized for AI consumption. It includes element references like `[ref=e2]`, includes snapshots of iframes inside the target and does not wait for a matching element, but fails immediately when no element matches. |


#### Allowed Values:

- `default`
- `ai`

#### Converted Types:

- string

---

### AriaSnapshotReturnType (Enum)

#### Documentation:



Defines the return type of the AriaSnapshot.


| Value | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `dict` | returns the snapshot as a dictionary. |
| `yaml` | returns the snapshot as a yaml string. |
| `parsed` | returns the snapshot as a tree of node dictionaries. |


`dict` loads the yaml as it is. Role, name and all annotations of an element stay inside the dictionary keys, for example `{'heading "Login Page" [level=1]': None}`.


`parsed` splits that information into separate keys. Every node has `role`, `name`, `text`, `props` and `children`, and its values are reachable both as `${node}[role]` and as `${node.role}`. Annotations without a value, like `[selected]`, become `True`, `[level=2]` becomes an integer and `box` uses the same keys as `Get BoundingBox`. The `/url` entry of a link is an annotation in Playwright, not an element, and therefore becomes the `url` property of the link instead of one of its children.


###### Examples

All outputs below come from the same element of the same page. It offers fourteen tag options; the examples stop after the fourth one:


```text
`New Browser`    chromium
`New Page`       https://robotframework-browser.org/keywords
${snapshot} =    `Get Aria Snapshot`    .rail-top
```

###### return_type=yaml (default)

```text
- text: Filter keywords
- searchbox "Filter keywords"
- group: Version 20.3.0
- text: Filter by tag
- combobox "Filter by tag":
```

### AssertionOperator (Enum)

#### Documentation:



Currently supported assertion operators are:


| Operator | Alternative Operators | Description | Validate Equivalent |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `==` | `equal`, `equals`, `should be` | Checks if returned value is equal to expected value. | `value == expected` |
| `!=` | `inequal`, `should not be` | Checks if returned value is not equal to expected value. | `value != expected` |
| `>` | `greater than` | Checks if returned value is greater than expected value. | `value > expected` |
| `>=` |  | Checks if returned value is greater than or equal to expected value. | `value >= expected` |
| `\<` | `less than` | Checks if returned value is less than expected value. | `value \< expected` |
| `\<=` |  | Checks if returned value is less than or equal to expected value. | `value \<= expected` |
| `*=` | `contains` | Checks if returned value contains expected value as substring. | `expected in value` |
|  | `not contains` | Checks if returned value does not contain expected value as substring. | `expected in value` |
| `^=` | `should start with`, `starts` | Checks if returned value starts with expected value. | `re.search(f"^{expected}", value)` |
| `$=` | `should end with`, `ends` | Checks if returned value ends with expected value. | `re.search(f"{expected}$", value)` |
| `matches` |  | Checks if given RegEx matches minimum once in returned value. | `re.search(expected, value)` |
| `validate` |  | Checks if given Python expression evaluates to `True`. |  |
| `evaluate` | `then` | When using this operator, the keyword does return the evaluated Python expression. |  |


There are three different possibilities what keyword returns when `matches` operator is used: string, tuple or dictionary. What keyword returns depends on how the RegEx is formed. If RegEx does not contain group(s), then keyword will return the string without modifications. If RegEx contains groups, meaning (...), then keyword will return a tuple. Each tuple item contains the text which is matched by the group. If there is group and group has a name, (?P\<name>...) syntax, then keyword returns a dictionary. In this case dictionary key is the group name and value contains the matched text. If there mix of groups and groups with names, then tuple is returned.


Currently supported formatters for assertions are:


| Formatter | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `normalize spaces` | Substitutes multiple spaces to single space from the value |
| `strip` | Removes spaces from the beginning and end of the value |
| `case insensitive` | Converts value to lower case before comparing |
| `apply to expected` | Applies rules also for the expected value |


Formatters are applied to the value before assertion is performed and keywords returns a value where rule is applied. Formatter is only applied to the value which keyword returns and not all rules are valid for all assertion operators. If `apply to expected` formatter is defined, then formatters are then formatter are also applied to expected value.


#### Allowed Values:

- `equal`
- `equals`
- `==`
- `should be`
- `inequal`
- `!=`
- `should not be`
- `less than`
- `<`
- `greater than`
- `>`
- `<=`
- `>=`
- `contains`
- `not contains`
- `*=`
- `starts`
- `^=`
- `should start with`
- `ends`
- `should end with`
- `$=`
- `matches`
- `validate`
- `then`
- `evaluate`

#### Converted Types:

- string

### AutoClosingLevel (Enum)

#### Documentation:



Controls when contexts and pages are closed during the test execution.


If automatic closing level is `TEST`, contexts and pages that are created during a single test are automatically closed when the test ends. Contexts and pages that are created during suite setup are closed when the suite teardown ends.


If automatic closing level is `SUITE`, all contexts and pages that are created during the test suite are closed when the suite teardown ends.


If automatic closing level is `MANUAL`, nothing is closed automatically while the test execution is ongoing. All browsers, context and pages are automatically closed when test execution ends.


If automatic closing level is `KEEP`, nothing is closed automatically while the test execution is ongoing. Also, nothing is closed when test execution ends, including the node process. Therefore, it is users responsibility to close all browsers, context and pages and ensure that all process that are left running after the test execution end are closed. This level is only intended for test case development and must not be used when running tests in CI or similar environments.


Automatic closing can be configured or switched off with the auto_closing_level library import parameter.


See: `Importing`


#### Allowed Values:

- `SUITE`
- `TEST`
- `MANUAL`
- `KEEP`

#### Converted Types:

- string

### boolean (Standard)

#### Documentation:



Strings `TRUE`, `YES`, `ON`, `1` and possible localization specific "true strings" are converted to Boolean `True`, the empty string, strings `FALSE`, `NO`, `OFF` and `0` and possibly localization specific "false strings" are converted to Boolean `False`, and the string `NONE` is converted to the Python `None` object. Other strings and all other values are passed as-is, allowing keywords to handle them specially if needed. All string comparisons are case-insensitive.


Examples: `TRUE` (converted to `True`), `off` (converted to `False`), `example` (used as-is)


#### Converted Types:

- string
- integer
- float
- None

### bytes (Standard)

#### Documentation:



Strings are converted to bytes so that each Unicode code point below 256 is directly mapped to a matching byte. Higher code points are not allowed. Robot Framework's `\xHH` escape syntax is convenient with bytes having non-printable values.


Examples: `good`, `hyvä` (same as `hyv\xE4`), `\x00` (the null byte)


Integers and sequences of integers are converted to matching bytes directly. They must be in range 0-255.


Examples: `0` (converted to the null byte), `[82, 70]` (converted to `RF`)


Support for integers and sequences of integers is new in Robot Framework 7.4.


#### Converted Types:

- string
- bytearray
- Sequence
- integer

### CookieSameSite (Enum)

#### Documentation:



Enum that defines the Cookie SameSite type.


It controls whether or not a cookie is sent with cross-site requests, providing some protection against cross-site request forgery attacks (CSRF).


The possible attribute values are:


| Value | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `Strict` | Means that the browser sends the cookie only for same-site requests, that is, requests originating from the same site that set the cookie. If a request originates from a different domain or scheme (even with the same domain), no cookies with the SameSite=Strict attribute are sent. |
| `Lax` | Means that the cookie is not sent on cross-site requests, such as on requests to load images or frames, but is sent when a user is navigating to the origin site from an external site (for example, when following a link). This is the default behavior if the SameSite attribute is not specified. |
| `None` | means that the browser sends the cookie with both cross-site and same-site requests. The Secure attribute must also be set when setting this value. |


See [MDN Set-Cookie](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Set-Cookie) for more information.


#### Allowed Values:

- `Strict`
- `Lax`
- `None`

#### Converted Types:

- string

### datetime (Standard)

#### Documentation:



String timestamps are expected to be in [ISO 8601](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601) like format `YYYY-MM-DD hh:mm:ss.mmmmmm`, where any non-digit character can be used as a separator or separators can be omitted altogether. Additionally, only the date part is mandatory, all possibly missing time components are considered to be zeros.


A special values `NOW` and `TODAY` (case-insensitive) can be used to get the current local `datetime`. This is new in Robot Framework 7.3.


Integers and floats are considered to represent seconds since the [Unix epoch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time).


Examples: `2022-02-09T16:39:43.632269`, `20220209 16:39`, `now`, `${1644417583.632269}` (Epoch time)


#### Converted Types:

- string
- integer
- float

### dictionary (Standard)

#### Documentation:



Strings must be Python [dictionary](https://docs.python.org/library/stdtypes.html#dict) literals. They are converted to actual dictionaries using the [ast.literal_eval](https://docs.python.org/library/ast.html#ast.literal_eval) function. They can contain any values `ast.literal_eval` supports, including dictionaries and other collections.


Any mapping is accepted and converted to a `dict`.


If the type has nested types like `dict[str, int]`, items are converted to those types automatically. This in new in Robot Framework 6.0.


Examples: `{'a': 1, 'b': 2}`, `{'key': 1, 'nested': {'key': 2}}`

### ElementState (Enum)

#### Documentation:



Enum that defines the state an element can have.


The following `states` are possible:


| State | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `attached` | to be present in DOM. |
| `detached` | to not be present in DOM. |
| `visible` | to have non or empty bounding box and no visibility:hidden. |
| `hidden` | to be detached from DOM, or have an empty bounding box or visibility:hidden. |
| `enabled` | to not be `disabled`. |
| `disabled` | to be `disabled`. Can be used on \<button>, \<fieldset>, \<input>, \<optgroup>, \<option>, \<select> and \<textarea>. |
| `editable` | to not be `readOnly`. |
| `readonly` | to be `readOnly`. Can be used on \<input> and \<textarea>. |
| `selected` | to be `selected`. Can be used on \<option>. |
| `deselected` | to not be `selected`. |
| `focused` | to be the `activeElement`. |
| `defocused` | to not be the `activeElement`. |
| `checked` | to be `checked`. Can be used on \<input>. |
| `unchecked` | to not be `checked`. |
| `stable` | to be both `visible` and `stable`. |

### integer (Standard)

#### Documentation:



Conversion is done using Python's [int](https://docs.python.org/library/functions.html#int) built-in function. Floating point numbers are accepted only if they can be represented as integers exactly. For example, `1.0` is accepted and `1.1` is not.


It is possible to use hexadecimal, octal and binary numbers by prefixing values with `0x`, `0o` and `0b`, respectively. Spaces and underscores can be used as visual separators for digit grouping purposes.


Examples: `42`, `-1`, `0b1010`, `10 000 000`, `0xBAD_C0FFEE`

### list (Standard)

#### Documentation:



Strings must be Python [list](https://docs.python.org/library/stdtypes.html#list) or [tuple](https://docs.python.org/library/stdtypes.html#tuple) literals. They are converted using the [ast.literal_eval](https://docs.python.org/library/ast.html#ast.literal_eval) function and possible tuples converted further to lists. They can contain any values `ast.literal_eval` supports, including lists and other collections.


If the argument is a list, it is used without conversion. Tuples and other sequences are converted to lists.


If the type has nested types like `list[int]`, items are converted to those types automatically.


Examples: `['one', 'two']`, `[('one', 1), ('two', 2)]`


Support to convert nested types is new in Robot Framework 6.0. Support for tuple literals is new in Robot Framework 7.4.


#### Converted Types:

- string
- Sequence

---

### Mapping (Standard)

#### Documentation:



Strings must be Python [dictionary](https://docs.python.org/library/stdtypes.html#dict) literals. They are converted to actual dictionaries using the [ast.literal_eval](https://docs.python.org/library/ast.html#ast.literal_eval) function. They can contain any values `ast.literal_eval` supports, including dictionaries and other collections.


Any mapping is accepted without conversion. An exception is that if the type is `MutableMapping`, immutable values are converted to `dict`.


If the type has nested types like `Mapping[str, int]`, items are converted to those types automatically. This in new in Robot Framework 6.0.


Examples: `{'a': 1, 'b': 2}`, `{'key': 1, 'nested': {'key': 2}}`


#### Converted Types:

- string
- Mapping

### PlaywrightLogTypes (Enum)

#### Documentation:

`disabled`: playwright-log.txt is not created at all. All node side logging is lost. `library`: Default, only logging from Browser library node side is written to the playwright-log.txt file. `playwright`: Also includes Playwright log messages to the playwright-log.txt file. `false`: Same as `library` and for backwards compatability. `true`: Same as `playwright` and for backwards compatibility.

`omitContent`: Optional setting to control whether to omit request content from the HAR. Default is False


`path`: Path on the filesystem to write the HAR file to. A relative path is relative to the output directory.

```text
${har} =    Create Dictionary     path=/path/to/har.file    omitContent=True
New Context    recordHar=${har}
```

### RecordVideo (TypedDict)

#### Documentation:



Enables Video recording


| Key | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `dir` | Folder of the videos. |
| `size` | `ViewportDimensions` of the videos. |
| `fps` | Frame rate of the videos. Defaults to 25. Firefox and WebKit record at most 25 frames per second. |
| `showActions` | Annotates the interacted elements in the videos, with the keys below. |


Keys of `showActions`:


| Key | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| `duration` | How long each annotation is shown, in milliseconds. Defaults to 500. |
| `position` | Position of the action title: `top-left`, `top`, `top-right` (default), `bottom-left`, `bottom` or `bottom-right`. |
| `cursor` | `pointer` (default) shows a mouse pointer that moves from one action point to the next, `none` shows no cursor. |
| `style` | CSS declarations of the annotations: `point` for the marker on the action point and `highlight` for the box over the element, both shown only when given, and `title` for the action title. |


Examples:


```text
 New Context  recordVideo={'dir':'videos', 'size':{'width':400, 'height':200}}
 New Context  recordVideo={'dir': 'd:/automation/video'}
 New Context  recordVideo={'showActions': {'position': 'bottom', 'style': {'title': 'font-size: 32px'}}}
```

#### Dictionary Structure:

```
{'dir': <str> # optional
 'size': <ViewportDimensions> # optional
 'fps': <int> # optional
 'showActions': <ShowActions> # optional
}
```

#### Converted Types:

- string
- Mapping

### RegExp (Custom)

#### Documentation:



Create a (JavaScript) RegExp object from a string.


The matcher must start with a slash and end with a slash and can be followed by flags.


Example: `/hello world/gi` Which is equivalent to `new RegExp("hello world", "gi")` in JavaScript.


Following flags are supported:


| Flag | Description |
| :--- | :--- |
| g | Global search. |
| i | Case-insensitive search. |
| m | Allows `^` and `$` to match newline characters. |
| s | Allows `.` to match newline characters. |
| u | "unicode"; treat a pattern as a sequence of unicode code points. |
| y | Perform a "sticky" search that matches starting at the current position in the target string. |


See [RegExp Object](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/RegExp) and [RegExp Guide](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Regular_expressions) for more information.

- string

When set to "css", screenshot will have a single pixel per each css pixel on the page. For high-dpi devices, this will keep screenshots small. Using "device" option will produce a single pixel per each device pixel, so screenshots of high-dpi devices will be twice as large or even larger.

### Scope (Enum)

#### Documentation:



Some keywords which manipulates library settings have a scope argument. With that scope argument one can set the "live time" of that setting. Available Scopes are: `Global`, `Suite` and `Test` / `Task`. Is a scope finished, this scoped setting, like timeout, will no longer be used and the previous higher scope setting applies again.


Live Times:


- A `Global` scope will live forever until it is overwritten by another Global scope. Or locally temporarily overridden by a more narrow scope.
- A `Suite` scope will locally override the Global scope and live until the end of the Suite within it is set, or if it is overwritten by a later setting with Global or same scope. Children suite does inherit the setting from the parent suite but also may have its own local Suite setting that then will be inherited to its children suites.
- A `Test` or `Task` scope will be inherited from its parent suite but when set, lives until the end of that particular test or task.


A new set higher order scope will always remove the lower order scope which may be in charge. So the setting of a Suite scope from a test, will set that scope to the robot file suite where that test is and removes the Test scope that may have been in place.


#### Allowed Values:

- `Global`
- `Suite`
- `Test`
- `Task`

#### Converted Types:

- string

### SelectAttribute (Enum)

#### Documentation:



Enum that defines the attribute of an \<option> element in a \<select>-list.


This defines by what attribute an option is selected/chosen.


```text
<select class="my_drop_down">
  <option value="0: Object">None</option>
  <option value="1: Object">Some</option>
  <option value="2: Object">Other</option>
</select>
```

`value` of the first option would be `0: Object`.


`label` / `text` both defines the innerText which would be `None` for first element.


`index` 0 indexed number of an option. Would be `0` for the first element.

### SelectionStrategy (Enum)

#### Documentation:



SelectionStrategy to be used. Refers to Playwrights `page.getBy***` functions. See [Playwright Locators](https://playwright.dev/docs/locators)


###### AltText

All images should have an alt attribute that describes the image. You can locate an image based on the text alternative using page.getByAltText().


For example, consider the following DOM structure.


```text
<img alt="playwright logo" src="/img/playwright-logo.svg" width="100" />
```

###### Label

Allows locating input elements by the text of the associated `\<label>` or `aria-labelledby` element, or by the `aria-label` attribute.


For example, this method will find inputs by label "Username" and "Password" in the following DOM:


```text
<input aria-label="Username">
<label for="password-input">Password:</label>
<input id="password-input">
```

###### Placeholder

Allows locating input elements by the placeholder text.


Example:


```text
<input type="email" placeholder="name@example.com" />
```

###### TestId

Locate element by the test id.


Currently only the exact attribute `data-testid` is supported.


Example:


```text
<button data-testid="directions">Itinéraire</button>
```

###### Text

Allows locating elements that contain given text.


Matching by text always normalizes whitespace, even with exact match. For example, it turns multiple spaces into one, turns line breaks into spaces and ignores leading and trailing whitespace. Input elements of the type button and submit are matched by their value instead of the text content. For example, locating by text "Log in" matches \<input type=button value="Log in">.


###### Title

Allows locating elements by their title attribute.


Example:


```text
<img alt="playwright logo" src="/img/playwright-logo.svg" title="Playwright" width="100" />
```

#### Allowed Values:

- `AltText`
- `Label`
- `Placeholder`
- `TestID`
- `Text`
- `Title`

#### Converted Types:

- string

`innerText`: Returns the element node.innerText value, which represents the rendered text content of a node and its descendants.

This trace can be activated with the `tracing` parameter of `New Context` keyword.


- `Full` All keyword calls are written to trace as groups even if they do not call Browser keywords.
- `Browser` Just Browser library keywords are written to the logs as groups.
- `Playwright` No additional keywords are logged, just the Playwright API calls.
